Just minutes before the crash, the co-pilot, 20-year-old Nathalia Filgueiras, reported encountering weather causing icing and "moderate turbulence." They asked to ascend to 37,000 feet, which was approved by Air Traffic Control. The plane then began descending quickly, with the co-pilot informing controllers, "We're descending 8,000 — Mayday, Mayday — we're descending 10,000 feet per minute.

One pilot has been identified as of this writing. Filgueiras was a Boca Raton resident who achieved her dream of a pilot's license while still in high school and had 1,300 hours of flying time under her belt. She was the one who made the final emergency calls as the jet went down. Another pilot was aboard the flight as well. It is unclear at this time who was at the controls of the jet when the crash occurred. All nine fatalities were passengers onboard the plane.

During a news conference Monday the NTSB officials said the crash created a debris field approximately a half mile by four-tenths of a mile, but it may be larger as there is evidence that shows the plane was likely breaking up prior to impact. They've asked members of the community who find debris to not move it and contact NTSB or local authorities to handle it. Officials also said that weather conditions are being considered as a major factor in the events that unfolded Sunday afternoon. More updates are expected to come in the following days.

In the plane's final transmissions, the plane was flying at an altitude of nearly 9,000 feet. The plane then nosedived, falling at 32,000 feet per minute according to CBS News , however, the NTSB said those numbers have not yet been determined or confirmed. Dashcam footage shared with multiple news outlets caught the moment of impact from the back of a moving vehicle on a divided motorway. Another dashcam video obtained by KCEN 6 News , showed the plane falling out of the sky some distance ahead of the vehicle before impact.

Witnesses to the crash told CBS News it sounded like a bomb went off when the jet hit the ground. Stephanie Platts, a resident at a neighboring mobile home community park, told The New York Times she was on her patio with her family when the plane hit, which sounded like a car crash. Her home caught fire from some of the raining debris.

Palm Beach County authorities were called to the scene where it was eventually confirmed that all nine passengers on board the business jet had died. Only one individual may have sustained injuries from the crash, who was adjacent to the scene, but officials have yet to confirm that injury.

This crash comes just months after an Amazon Air cargo plane killed five people after landing late on a Miami runway. Weeks later, a small yellow airplane narrowly missed hitting a postal van while making an emergency landing on an Illinois highway, leaving no crashes or injuries behind.

article_paragraphs: Nothing says Neue Klasse like using AI slop to bash a '90s economy sedan

Mercedes-Benz might be BMW's biggest rival, but the Bavarian automaker chose a different target on its latest social media post. The company shared a photo of a de-badged 1991 Toyota Corolla on Instagram, labeling it as "boring" design compared to the 2027 BMW X5. Predictably, things didn't go well, and the comment section had plenty to say — both in support of the Toyota and scathing the BMW's design.

The first photo is an AI-generated image of a '90s model without an emblem, but it appears to depict a seventh-generation Corolla (E100), which was in production from 1991 through 1997. The classic model features halogen headlights, and an unpainted plastic finish for the bumper, grille, and mirrors. Besides the missing Toyota badge, the indicators have been digitally removed from the front bumper, possibly in a minimal effort to avoid any copyright infringement.

The second photo shows the front end of the all-new BMW X5 G65 , and it features the M Sport package with the distinct bumper intakes. The caption for the post reads: "We don't just design cars. We give them character. Unmistakably BMW. Made Different. To Feel Different."

Not surprisingly, BMW's feeble attempt to flex the Neue Klasse styling language of the new X5 against a 36-year-old economy sedan didn't resonate with the audience. In fact, the backfire in the comments section is pretty entertaining. From what we read, the majority of commenters rushed to defend the humble Toyota, and some even suggest that that the labels ought to be reversed, praising the unpretentious design and durability of the Japanese classic. One commenter said: "No not boring, classic," while others pointed out the automakers social media team still had time to delete the post.

Many critics took aim at the Neue Klasse model, and some even accused BMW of deploying "rage bait" marketing tactics. Still, there were a few loyal fans who voiced support for the German brand, albeit the older models such as the E30 and E39. An account with no profile picture and no posts said, "You create and build cars that fans and enthusiast would love to test drive and own . That is just facts . Me and many others have the same opinion ." To which BMW responded: "Appreciate that, Roy! There's a lot of work behind making a BMW feel like a BMW."

Whether the post was intended as lighthearted banter or calculated social engagement, the audience made its stance loud and clear. Next time, BMW should pick a fight with premium rivals from the same era if they want to be taken seriously.

Revealed in 2006 and brought to market in 2008, the Tesla Roadster earned critical plaudits for being the first production EV to offer a usable driving range (of up to 244 miles). Performance was also noteworthy, as the Lotus Elise-based electric sports car could sprint to 60 mph in less than four seconds, thanks to its gobs of instant electric torque. With this, the Roadster not only won over buyers — a total of 2,450 during its lifetime — but also dispelled preconceived notions about electric cars being slow and impractical.

Then again, being a groundbreaker doesn't come cheap, as the 2008 Tesla Roadster's price shows. The luxury sports car went on sale for $98,000, which is equivalent to around $153,000 in 2026, and today, the amount you'll need to pay for a concours condition example will be close to the car's original MSRP. According to Hagerty , concours Roadsters carry eye-watering valuations of between $85,633 and $97,767, while examples in excellent condition start at a shade over $66,000 and top out at $79,567. If you're bargain hunting and would rather have something cheaper, those in good condition sell from $45,567 to $58,967, while fair-condition Roadsters are available for even less, at between $27,167 and $39,433.

Several factors contribute to the original Tesla Roadster's impressive value retention, with brand kudos, its reputation as the car that brought EVs into the mainstream, and the symbolic weight it carries as the car that launched Tesla being some of the biggest. Beyond its historical legacy, the original Roadster enjoys relative rarity, considering Tesla only made 2,450 units between the 2008 and 2012 model years. This means that used models are hard to come by, even on leading online marketplaces.

A quick glance at what's currently available on CarGurus shows a lone 19,000-mile example priced at $81,600, and it does look like prices are around this range at the moment. One recently went for $77,000 on Bring a Trailer . So, while they fetch good money for owners whenever they appear on the market, Tesla Roadsters usually sell significantly below their new price in 2008. This is not to say all Roadsters have depreciated. The limited-edition "Signature One Hundred" models, for example, have become astronomically valuable. We've already seen a Tesla Roadster with under 1,000 miles sell for $250,000 , and plenty of other Roadsters like it have done well over the past few years, too, fetching well over $100,000 from buyers.

Heck, even the regular Roadsters have been pretty pricey in the past, too. According to Hagerty's data, these cars were at their high point back in 2023 when concours-perfect models fetched around $164,000, while examples in excellent condition floated around for $131,000. In good condition, Roadsters charged $95,300 then, with models in fair condition costing $61,300.

title: Yamaha Refuses To Race In Qatar Despite MotoGP's Penalty Threats
raw_summary: Despite concerns that President Donald Trump will restart hostilities in the U.S. war against Iran after the midterm elections, MotoGP must go on. But Yamaha announced Sunday that it will not travel to the Lusail International Circuit for next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix . The Japanese manufacturer cited a company-wide policy currently barring travel to the Middle East. In response, MotoGP threatened Yamaha with contractual and sporting implications. Yamaha's absence means that its two factory motorcycles and Pramac's two satellite bikes will not compete in Qatar. The company stated, "This decision reflects Yamaha's assessment of the information currently available and is independent of the measures implemented by MotoGP Group and the event organizer." While the safety of the team's employees should be paramount, Yamaha didn't have much to lose competitively. The factory team and Pramac are in the last two spots in the teams' standings. Yamaha expects to return for the next round in Portugal, but the manufacturer might not be allowed to rejoin.

The Japanese manufacturer cited a company-wide policy currently barring travel to the Middle East. In response, MotoGP threatened Yamaha with contractual and sporting implications.

Yamaha's absence means that its two factory motorcycles and Pramac's two satellite bikes will not compete in Qatar. The company stated, "This decision reflects Yamaha's assessment of the information currently available and is independent of the measures implemented by MotoGP Group and the event organizer." While the safety of the team's employees should be paramount, Yamaha didn't have much to lose competitively. The factory team and Pramac are in the last two spots in the teams' standings. Yamaha expects to return for the next round in Portugal, but the manufacturer might not be allowed to rejoin.

MotoGP's response offered few details about the implied financial and competitive consequences, but the championship's organizers stated that every other team committed to racing in Qatar. Don't be deceived by the release, though. The riders have been far from content with the situation they have been forced into.

Riders first held a secret meeting on the matter at Phillip Island ahead of the Australian Grand Prix. It's safe to say management didn't take it well. Last week, The Race reported that MotoGP refused to even give the riders a meeting room at Sepang last weekend. Instead, they reconvened inside Yamaha hospitality. MotoGP also threatened to ban any riders who boycott Qatar from the final two rounds in Portugal and Spain. According to Motorsport.com , outgoing Pramac rider Jack Miller revealed:

"I don't want to go. Like everybody. There's 19 of us that don't want to go there. I don't think we should be racing like that. We've made our opinion very clear on that. We'll see what the decision is.

As riders, we've united and done the best we can, and threatened the best we can with what ammunition we have. Not only for us as riders, but also other people in the championship. You speak to 50% of the paddock, nobody wants to go. I don't understand why we need to. I don't understand."

Some riders are finding their own ways out of racing in Qatar without consequences. Alex Marquez elected to undergo surgery to repair his right shoulder, which he injured in May. He aims to miss only Qatar. It wouldn't be surprising if other riders with lingering injuries also withdraw.

No matter what assurances MotoGP made to all 22 riders, there's no way it could guarantee everyone's safe passage out of Qatar should things escalate in the region further. There are hundreds of people who work in the paddock across MotoGP, Moto2 and Moto3. Organizers also can't prevent the worst-case scenario of Lusail Circuit itself being the target of an Iranian drone or missile strike, and the track sits 27 miles away from Al Udeid Air Base, the largest U.S. military base in the Middle East.

article_paragraphs: Does every off-road vehicle need portal axles? Not exactly, but they are nice to have

The Lexus GX 550 is big, brutish, and bold, combining on-road comfort and presence with strong off-road abilities. For this year's SEMA Show, Mountain Yotas has leaned into the GX's rugged side and built the MTN 550 Recon. It makes a regular GX 550 look tame and appears capable of easily traversing even the most difficult of terrain.

Arguably the most significant modification is the fitment of custom black anodized 74Weld portal axles. The Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6 of 2013 was one of the first high-end off-roaders with portal axles, and they help to significantly boost ground clearance – a key objective of this build. Other upgrades include Fox Live Valve shocks, billet upper control arms, billet rear links, and Fox Live Valve shocks at all four corners.

Mountain Yotas has then bolted on a set of forged beadlock wheels with huge 40-inch Mickey Thompson tires and fitted a Hardblock 4x4 front locker, combined with the standard center and rear locking differentials. Helping to keep all the SUV's important mechanical components safe from rock strikes are steel skid plates running along the length of the underside. A set of custom front and rear bumpers both revamps the look of the GX and maximizes approach and departure angles.

The upgrades don't stop here . The MTN 550 Recon boasts rock sliders, a Warn EVO winch, and stainless steel fender flares, unlike the cheap plastic fenders most off-road-focused SUVs and pickups use. It also has loads of new LED driving lights, including in the front brush bar and on the roof. Speaking of the roof, it includes a custom steel rack. A pair of stainless steel snorkels also help this GX 550's twin-turbocharged 3.4-liter V6 breathe during deep water crossings. The upgrades are so comprehensive that they even installed thermal cameras alongside ballistic-armored door panels.

Mountain Yotas opted not to mess with the GX's fabulous V6 engine, though they did craft a side-exit stainless steel exhaust system. As we discovered while driving the GX last year , it sounds fabulous in standard guise, so this one must sound absolutely insane.

The interior has been altered quite significantly. The seats and door panels are now trimmed in high-end Italian leather with genuine Alcantara accents found throughout. Mountain Yotas has added color with red contrast stitching and red Alcantara door trims, and installed a custom roof dash console to control all the auxiliary lights and the Starlink attached to the roof. A Rolls-Royce-inspired Starlight headliner boosts the GX's sense of luxury.

title: Swarm Of Electric Trucks Coming To US (Battery Swapping Included?)
raw_summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk famously ditched the idea of EV battery swapping back in 2015 after a brief experiment. That pretty much laid the idea to rest here in the US, but other EV stakeholders soldiered on. The latest example is the Australian firm Janus Electric, which is bringing its Class 8 heavy duty electric truck conversions to North America. Janus offers a battery-as-a-service model that includes both charging and swapping…so, is battery swapping finally coming here to the US?. Battery swapping for two-wheelers and larger EVs is commonplace in some overseas markets, with industry leader Nio being one example. So far, though, swapping stations for e-bikes are the only sign of emerging activity in the US.
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk famously ditched the idea of EV battery swapping back in 2015 after a brief experiment. That pretty much laid the idea to rest here in the US, but other EV stakeholders soldiered on. The latest example is the Australian firm Janus Electric, which is bringing its Class 8 heavy duty electric truck conversions to North America.
article_paragraphs: Tesla CEO Elon Musk famously ditched the idea of EV battery swapping back in 2015 after a brief experiment. That pretty much laid the idea to rest here in the US, but other EV stakeholders soldiered on. The latest example is the Australian firm Janus Electric, which is bringing its Class 8 heavy duty electric truck conversions to North America. Janus offers a battery-as-a-service model that includes both charging and swapping…so, is battery swapping finally coming here to the US?.

Battery swapping for two-wheelers and larger EVs is commonplace in some overseas markets, with industry leader Nio being one example. So far, though, swapping stations for e-bikes are the only sign of emerging activity in the US.

Musk’s opinion aside, a modern battery swapping station can change a spent electric car battery for a fresh one in just a few minutes, or less time than it takes to drive through an automated car wash. On the other hand, considering today’s EV fast charging technology, battery swapping is somewhat less relevant to passenger cars and other light duty vehicles. Access to home charging is another factor that can limit the appeal of driving to a battery swapping station for a refresh.

Electric trucks, though, are another kettle of fish. Every minute counts in the fast paced transportation industry. Waiting in line for an EV charging station to free up is a non-starter, and then there’s the charging time. Even the much-heralded Tesla Semi Class 8 truck can take hours to reach a full charge overnight, though the truck is reported to achieve 60-70% charge in as little as 30-45 minutes at fast charging stations.

The time factor explains why battery swapping for trucks is appearing in overseas markets. The seeds of change have also begun to sprout up in the US, where the the diesel-to-electric conversion field is beginning to offer some opportunities. Last summer, for example, the US startup Revoy (formerly SixWheels) announced a swappable battery retrofit for Class 8 diesel trucks . The retrofit consists of a battery unit inserted between the cab and the trailer, which can be swapped out in a matter of minutes. The unit does not replace the engine, but it reportedly cuts diesel emissions by up to 85%, with a 95% fuel savings aided by regenerative braking.

The US Army is also dipping a toe in the conversion field with “idling kits,” which are batteries powerful enough to run on-board equipment for military vehicles in near silence, without the giveaway noise and heat signature involved in idling the vehicle’s engine . No word yet on whether or not swap-outs will be part of the picture, but the technology pieces are in place.

So much for the current state of affairs. Last week a full diesel-to-electric conversion opportunity suddenly appeared when the Canadian lithium-ion battery specialist Electrovaya announced a new $26 million diesel-to-electric supply agreement with the Janus that leverages Electrovaya’s proprietary “Infinity Battery Technology , a durable system compatible with daily swapping cycles for Class 8 trucks.

The $26 million agreement represents just the initial phase of orders for the US and Canadian markets. “Electrovaya has also agreed to invest approximately $1.4 million in Janus for up to 4.2 million shares, together with up to 6.3 million warrants,” Electrovaya noted, indicating a long term partnership allowing plenty of room for scaleup.

title: Chevy Reportedly Axes Plans for the Corvette SUV and EV
raw_summary: The imagined future of a broad lineup of Corvette-badged SUVs, sedans, and electric vehicles that some of us dreamed about—or perhaps dreaded—is no longer set to become a reality. GM’s long-rumored plans to build out the Corvette brand as a broader lineup have been shelved, according to a report by GM Authority citing sources within the company. We’ve been discussing the possibility of a Corvette SUV for years now, and this Porsche Cayenne –fighting model appears to be the most significant casualty of this news. Electric power had also been discussed for a future Corvette, and Chevrolet does currently offer two hybrid powertrains in the C8 Corvette, but it now sounds like GM’s upcoming electric-vehicle platforms won’t be making their way into any models with a Corvette badge. The report even mentions rumors of a four-door Corvette sedan that now isn’t likely to ever see the light of day.

title: Track-Optimized Fluidity: We Drive the 2027 Ariel Atom 4RR
raw_summary: When the Ariel Atom launched around the turn of the millennium, probably no one imagined that the lightweight British track car would evolve into the 4RR model of today—a 525-hp road-legal range topper based on the fourth-generation Atom and launched to celebrate the original’s 25th anniversary. In fact, the roughly 1500-pound “Double R” might be hard for U.S. buyers to conceive of, as only some lesser Ariel vehicles had been available stateside under a manufacturing licensing arrangement. An exclusive new deal between Ariel and long-standing U.S. distributor Forman Motorworks changes that, with all Ariels and optional equipment now available to order via Forman for U.K. factory build slots. Customer deliveries in the U.S. are planned to start next summer.

article_paragraphs: When the Ariel Atom launched around the turn of the millennium, probably no one imagined that the lightweight British track car would evolve into the 4RR model of today—a 525-hp road-legal range topper based on the fourth-generation Atom and launched to celebrate the original’s 25th anniversary. In fact, the roughly 1500-pound “Double R” might be hard for U.S. buyers to conceive of, as only some lesser Ariel vehicles had been available stateside under a manufacturing licensing arrangement.

An exclusive new deal between Ariel and long-standing U.S. distributor Forman Motorworks changes that, with all Ariels and optional equipment now available to order via Forman for U.K. factory build slots. Customer deliveries in the U.S. are planned to start next summer.

The lineup includes the 4RR seen here, which is both the most powerful Atom ever and the most expensive at £208,000 in the U.K. (U.S. prices have yet to be confirmed, but we’d estimate $325,000.) That’s more than double the price of a very generously optioned 400-hp 4R model.

Lower yourself into the Atom’s molded composite driving seat, thumb the start button, and feel the hand-built Civic Type R –derived turbo four-cylinder fizz through the steel-tube-frame chassis. Admittedly, the thought of blasting over the hedged lanes near Ariel’s rural base in Somerset, England, is more than a little intimidating. Yet even as the 4RR accelerates ferociously and telegraphs mechanical and road-surface detail like few other cars can, the big surprise is just how calm this extreme Atom feels.

Whether it’s the car’s refusal to be upset by midcorner bumps and awkward road cambers, or the drivability of the highly boosted turbo four, there’s an unexpected maturity and polish at play here. Even the Quaife six-speed sequential transmission can be soothed with a gentle brush of the clutch pedal. A handful of miles in, and our trepidation has already melted away.

Two things explain the 4RR’s fine road manners. The first is the clearly accomplished setup work overseen by race driver and former Top Gear Stig Phil Keen, and the second is some very expensive engineering.

raw_title: Driving A 43-Horsepower Geo Metro Convertible From New York To Los Angeles Looks Really Miserable
title: Driving A 43-Horsepower Geo Metro Convertible From New York To Los Angeles Looks Really Miserable
raw_summary: The Geo Metro Convertible is one of the silliest cars ever sold in America. The Metro hatchback was already a misfit on American roads, with its microscopic 1.0-liter three-cylinder engine, 1,600-pound curb weight, and $7,000-ish starting price. It was a General Motors rebadge of a Suzuki Swift, and it almost immediately became the butt of every automotive joke. There was no logical reason, then, for any engineer to lop off its roof and turn it into a convertible, but that didn't stop it from happening, and honestly I'm grateful GM sold them anyway. I doubt GM ever imagined that a YouTuber would end up driving one from New York to Los Angeles 34 years after it was built, but that's just what Mitchell Kohrmann did in his latest video . When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

It was a General Motors rebadge of a Suzuki Swift, and it almost immediately became the butt of every automotive joke. There was no logical reason, then, for any engineer to lop off its roof and turn it into a convertible, but that didn't stop it from happening, and honestly I'm grateful GM sold them anyway. I doubt GM ever imagined that a YouTuber would end up driving one from New York to Los Angeles 34 years after it was built, but that's just what Mitchell Kohrmann did in his latest video .

When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

I had never seen any of Kohrmann's videos before watching this one, but looking at his other uploads, he's no stranger to long drives, including a 10,050-mile drive to the Arctic Ocean in a Touareg V10 diesel , and a 6,500-mile drive in a V10 Audi S8. Those are both leather-lined luxury cruisers, though, and going from that to a vinyl-topped three-cylinder economy car must feel like quite the downgrade. With just 43 horsepower, Kohrmann ends up keeping the little Metro's gas pedal in contact with the floor a lot more than I expected.

The calamities begin before he even starts his journey, since he realized the Geo's tires may have looked fine at first, but they were utterly ancient, so he had to source some 155/80R13 tires at the last minute. Fortunately he finds some that will fit, and sets off on the drive. Predictably, the drive into and out of Manhattan involves navigating excruciating traffic jams, but once he gets out away from New York, he starts covering more ground.

This video is about 1.5 hours long, and includes lots of POV shots as well as breakdown and repair content and tons of beautiful scenery. Kohrmann initially intended to attempt to beat some sub-1.0-liter engine Cannonball Run record of 48 hours, 9 minutes and 53 seconds that was set in 1964 by a Sunbeam Imp, but he gives up on that after a series of setbacks. Regardless, he still completes the journey in 49 hours, 11 minutes and 18 seconds, after a harrowing journey filled with twists, turns, breakdowns, and hellish traffic jams. I think it's worth a watch. Cheers to you, Mitchell, for following through on what looks like an utterly miserable journey, but a really cool video.

article_paragraphs: Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.
The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.
Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.
The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.
Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.
It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

title: Fridge Hacking In Europe Making Case For Slate In United States
raw_summary: AI-enabled hacking agents guarantee that a massive cyberattack is just a matter of when, not if Supermarkets across Europe are being hit by cyberattacks on their fridges. article_paragraphs: AI-enabled hacking agents guarantee that a massive cyberattack is just a matter of when, not if

Supermarkets across Europe are being hit by cyberattacks on their fridges. These attacks are preventing refrigerators and coolers from cooling, causing food to spoil and costing stores large sums. One of the main questions being asked is: Why are fridges connected to the internet anyway?

While some speculate this is part of a hybrid warfare campaign by Russian hackers, the Kremlin has denied involvement. What is known, for sure, is that IT systems are often vulnerable to attack, and the proliferation of artificial intelligence and tools built around AI makes it easier than ever to hack and exploit systems. Do you remember when every piece of technology that ran PHP needed updating? That was an exploit found via AI tools.

Additionally, automakers are focusing even more on the connected car experience. A couple of weeks ago, General Motors highlighted plans to launch OnStar AI and use cloud services to store things like dash cam footage. Even though the footage will be end-to-end encrypted, it may still seem unnecessary. Just today, Ford announced its new privacy policy for connected vehicles , assuring us it'll protect our data and let us opt out of certain features if we choose.

That brings me to Slate Auto. If this is the first time you've heard about Slate , congratulations on coming out from that rock you live under. Simply put, this back-to-basics pickup truck is the polar opposite of what other automakers are doing with their connected vehicles. The planned launch of this affordable, all-electric truck couldn't be timed any better as U.S. gas prices continue to set records for all the wrong reasons.

Despite being advanced EVs, Slate trucks feature that old-school simplicity. There is no infotainment standard, and even remote climate control requires a telematics module that costs extra. If you leave your home without your phone, your truck can't connect to anything while you're out and about. Presumably, some data is stored that a service department can recover, but that requires hooking your truck up to a service computer, which not everyone has.

Now, do people actually want a truck with two doors, crank windows, and bare-bones creature comforts? That's yet to be seen. With the increase in AI-enabled hacking, a massive automotive data breach isn't a matter of if, but when. And we're not hearing enough from automakers about how they are working to protect us from that — or something even worse — when they talk about the brave new world these connected vehicles will usher in. I, for one, want to know more about that before I embrace an even more connected future.

title: Everything we learned from F1's 2026 Mexican Grand Prix
raw_summary: Formula 1’s new champion was crowned amid an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix weekend that taught us plenty. It's now a pattern of behaviour, and this time it cost Ferrari a very likely win and a probable 1-2. Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked. It's now a pattern of behaviour, and this time it cost Ferrari a very likely win and a probable 1-2. Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1’s new champion was crowned amid an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix weekend that taught us plenty.

It's now a pattern of behaviour, and this time it cost Ferrari a very likely win and a probable 1-2. Charles Leclerc's attack on Lewis Hamilton on lap one and Hamilton's response to it opened a door through which Max Verstappen happily walked. But it should never have been open at all had Ferrari had a robust team tactics plan in place - or, much more importantly given what unfolded, any hope of trusting its drivers to smoothly execute it.

That lack of trust was the main takeaway from just how the Ferrari situation kept unspooling as Sunday night progressed in Mexico. Every new interview Fred Vasseur did sounded more exasperated. Hamilton's condemnation of Leclerc's approach to intra-team racing in general got more blunt as the post-race press conference went on.
"I think it's a mentality thing. It's like 'do or die - either I win or none of us do', and it shouldn't be that. It should be us getting that 1-2," was Hamilton's most damning line.

But it had also been Hamilton calling for the stewards to penalise Leclerc in the race at a point where Red Bull would have been the direct beneficiary. And they'd both outbraked themselves while fixated on beating each other on lap one. Meanwhile, Leclerc just tried to redirect any angst towards the circuit layout (how careless of the organisers not to barrier-line the track so he couldn't corner cut to overtake his team-mate) and suggest the intra-team element didn't really seem much of a "talking point".

This is a mess. It can be plastered over with some talks or new guidelines. But fundamentally these are two drivers who don't trust each other to have the team's best interests at heart, and who are giving their team little reason to trust them. - Matt Beer
F1 can feel quite fortunate that Leclerc didn’t win the race because he cut the track to gain the race lead.

Thankfully for F1, Verstappen was able to stay just within five seconds of Leclerc and Red Bull cleverly pitted him immediately when Leclerc served his penalty to ensure Verstappen got track position.

raw_summary: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season. The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
summary: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season. The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has explained why he is choosing not to run with the title winner's #1 on his car next season.
The Italian made history at the Mexican Grand Prix as he became the youngest driver to ever win the crown at the age of 20.
That feat gives him the opportunity if he chooses to run with the #1 on his car next season, as 2025 champion Lando Norris has done this season.
However, Antonelli has said that he will stick with his current #12 - as that number has personal significance for him, plus he has not had the best of luck in the past when he has run with #1.
Antonelli chose #12 as his F1 race number to honour his hero Ayrton Senna, who raced with it during his Lotus years from 1985-87 as well as in his first title-winning campaign with McLaren in 1988.

Asked whether he would take up the option of running #1, Antonelli said: "I'll stay with #12 because, obviously, it's a very special number for me, but also it's a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble.
"I feel like by keeping #12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve.
"And also, to be honest, I'm very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I put it, it went extremely badly. So one more reason to stay with #12."

This bespoke ADX has been built in partnership with Vans athlete Coco Zurita and leans into tuning culture and the world of BMX bikes. It makes the ADX look more striking without going overboard, and uses the fabric found in Vans shoes. While the special ADX looks fitting of a Type R or Type S badge, it doesn't have any major mechanical upgrades.

Most of the design team's efforts have been focused on transforming the SUV's look. They've done this by fitting a custom carbon fiber splitter and a set of flared wheel arches at the front and rear. The ADX also includes distinctive side skirts, motorsport-inspired wing mirrors, a rear diffuser, and a custom exhaust. As Zurita is best known as a BMX rider, the Acura also includes a section in the cargo area to store and display a bike. Other tweaks include a rear bar, black graphics, and Rotiform aero disc wheels wrapped in Yokohama Advan Sport V105 tires.

The interior also differs significantly from a standard ADX, with racing seats and a steering wheel from Sparco, custom red upholstery, a racing harness, rear-seat delete, and white and black checkered fabric. If only this ADX was fitted with the turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder from the Honda Civic Type R and Acura Integra Type S.

Acura is investing heavily in a lineup of new and refreshed SUVs in the U.S. The two most significant models are a three-row flagship SUV to slot above the MDX and a new adventure-ready SUV based on the Honda Passport TrailSport. Though an all-new ADX isn't in the cards, CarScoops recently reported that a host of updated Acura SUVs are in the works, including the ADX. We doubt this will be a version that shares a resemblance to the CZ-77 Concept, as a more obvious addition to the ADX lineup would be a hybrid model that could share its powertrain with the Honda Civic Hybrid.

article_paragraphs: BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.
The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.
BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.
To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.

BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.
According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.
Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.

raw_summary: Germany’s hydrogen backbone achieved a genuine milestone on August 4, 2026. summary: Germany’s hydrogen backbone achieved a genuine milestone on August 4, 2026. RWE and its partners announced that renewable hydrogen produced during commissioning at Lingen had reached Marl Chemical Park , roughly 120 kilometres away. Electrolysers, converted natural gas pipelines and industrial receiving infrastructure were working together.
article_paragraphs: Germany’s hydrogen backbone achieved a genuine milestone on August 4, 2026. RWE and its partners announced that renewable hydrogen produced during commissioning at Lingen had reached Marl Chemical Park , roughly 120 kilometres away. Electrolysers, converted natural gas pipelines and industrial receiving infrastructure were working together.

The GET H2 consortium deserves credit for getting the equipment operating. But completing a hydrogen pipeline and establishing an economically competitive market for the hydrogen moving through it are different achievements.

The announcement did not disclose the quantity received at Marl, the price paid by an industrial customer or which existing hydrogen production was displaced. The English release describes hydrogen being available for industrial use, while the German release says it was used. Neither provides the industrial mass balance needed to determine the actual emissions benefit. The network also contained hydrogen from earlier commissioning activities, which makes tracing individual molecules through the pipeline less useful than measuring what changed at the receiving industrial facilities.

Marl is hardly a new hydrogen customer. The chemical park has used hydrogen for decades in integrated production processes. Providing another source may be useful, especially where renewable hydrogen replaces fossil-derived supply, but existing demand does not automatically become commercially viable demand for a considerably more expensive feedstock.

The larger infrastructure ambition makes that distinction important. Germany’s approved hydrogen core network covers 9,040 kilometres and has expected investment costs of €18.9 billion. Much of the network will use converted natural gas pipelines. These are approved plans and anticipated investments, not evidence that the entire network has been built or that future customers have committed to using it.

There are genuine industrial commitments. RWE has a 15-year agreement with TotalEnergies to supply approximately 30,000 tonnes of renewable hydrogen annually to the Leuna refinery from 2030. That provides a named customer, volume and contract period. The price is undisclosed, and European fuel regulations help create demand for renewable hydrogen in refining.

That is a much stronger commercial signal than commissioning a pipeline. The question is how many comparable customers exist, what they can afford and whether their businesses will continue using hydrogen over the decades required to recover infrastructure investments.

The wider European outlook has become less optimistic. ENTSOG’s October 2026 draft assessment reduced its 2030 hydrogen demand assumption from 620 TWh to 335 TWh, a 46% reduction from its 2024 assessment. Its 2040 assumption fell 33%, from 1,929 TWh to 1,296 TWh. These are changes to European planning scenarios, not measurements of declining actual hydrogen consumption, but they matter when infrastructure economics depend on demand growth.

raw_title: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
title: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
raw_summary: There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed. Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. article_paragraphs: There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.

Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .

Theoretically, things are only going to get better from here, sales-wise, with the only currently available R2 clocking in at $59,485, including destination. Eventually, a $55,485 Premium trim and $46,485 base model will join its ranks , but the only information we've got is "coming late 2026" and "coming spring 2027," respectively. Of course, even the most expensive R2 is a hell of a lot cheaper than the R1S and R1T, which both start well north of $80,000.

And good news keeps coming, because last week, Scaringe said he was "very confident" Rivian would hit an autonomy milestone this year that would unlock a quarter-billion-dollar tranche of investment money from Uber. That's part of an up-to $1.25 billion investment the rideshare company is making in the automaker through 2031, according to Reuters. It includes an initial $300 million and is contingent on several autonomy milestones. However, Rivian hasn't said exactly what those milestones are. Don't worry, though. Scaringe says Rivian is "right on time."

We do know that the partnership between Uber and Rivian targets the 2028 launch of a driverless R2 robotaxi on Uber's network — starting in a handful of cities and then expanding to about 25 over the next year and a half. Clearly, Rivian is aiming its R2 robotaxi directly at the Tesla Cybercab.

It needs to work, too. As Reuters points out, both the R2's success and the Uber partnership are imperative for making Rivian stick as a company. It's doing pretty well right now, don't get me wrong, but it's still burning through cash like the Bouvier Beale family, and it's looking for any way to narrow those losses.

No matter how you slice it, Rivian is truly showing it's a company that has the ability to stick around and be viable. Once R2 production is fully ramped up and the R3 is introduced, who knows where it could end up? All it needs to do is get that pesky cash burn problem under control.

article_paragraphs: Jackery just launched the Explorer 100D portable power station. This is Jackery’s smallest battery, giving a new level of versatility to power many of the devices people rely on most. Meanwhile, it integrates the durability and safety people expect from Jackery’s larger models into a compact case.

The Explorer 100D has a capacity of 96 Wh (30,000mAh) which puts it just below the carryon limit for domestic and international flights. Meanwhile, up to 158 W of output is more than enough to charge a laptop. The 100D is compatible with advanced protocols including AVS, PD 3.1 and PPS, providing precise charging, particularly for Apple products.

The Explorer 100D measures 4.6” X 3.4” X 3.4”(11.6 X 8.3 cm X 8.5 cm), or about the size of a softball. It weighs 1.87 lbs. (850 g). This is a bit larger than the typical power bank, but much smaller than the typical solar generator. It is also smaller and lighter than the Explorer 100 Plus that it replaces, while also increasing in power output.

On the test sample model, I found the form factor very convenient. It is not small enough to fit in your pants pocket, but the rectangular case with rounded corners was easy to fit in a backpack or carryon bag. A cloth handle makes it easy to hold, and a shoulder strap is available. I had a credentials lanyard from a previous media event on hand, and it worked fine as a strap for the lightweight battery.

On the front of the battery are two 140 W USB-C ports and an 18 W USB-A port. The left USB-C port can both charge the battery and discharge to another device. The battery can also be discharged through the other two ports while it charges. The battery does not come with a charger, although a USB-C cable is provided. I was able to charge the Explorer 100D on a wide range of chargers, although lower powered chargers take a while to charge the large capacity battery.

The front display default shows battery charge percentage as well as input and output power. However, you can switch the display to also show power output to each port or battery health, cycles and temperature.

Unlike some of Jackery’s larger batteries, the 100D does not have cooling fans or vents in the case. The LFP battery is rated for 3000 full charge cycles, good for 8 years of daily use. This is far more durable than many Li-ion power banks, which commonly only offer a few hundred charge cycles. It is also a 50% improvement over the previous Explorer 100 Plus model that it replaces. Of note, while this model does comply with China’s strict CCC (China Compulsory Certification), the logo was not printed on the test model I received, although that may change in the future. Without the logo present, it could be taken away if travelling in China. However, the battery did have FCC and SGS certification printed on it, which are more relevant to most US customers.

The portable battery can function as a solar generator by accepting direct solar input up to 100 W. This makes it a bit different than many power banks. Solar panels connect through the USB-C charge port. which may require the purchase of an adaptor, depending on the panel used. Jackery’s lightweight, folding SolarSaga 100 Air could charge the battery in less than two hours. The battery can also take 12 V or 24V input from a car, boat or RV. Using a traditional USB-C charger, the Explorer 100D can accept up to 140 W of input power.

title: What was Antonelli's best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say
raw_summary: Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process.
summary: Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process.
article_paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best?
Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process.
Our writers have picked out the moments they believe turned the Italian from a contender into a world champion in waiting.

It may sound odd to pick one of Antonelli's few defeats against Russell, but his runner-up spot to the Briton at the season opener in Melbourne showed me the first tranche of evidence that the Antonelli who had rocked up Australia wasn't the same insecure rookie who had struggled through spells of 2025.

The Albert Park weekend was actually one of Antonelli's more challenging weekends, suffering a heavy 25G crash in FP3 that looked set to derail his weekend. It may have done a year prior, but this time the young Italian stayed cool and collected. And as Mercedes was able to pull off a full rebuild just in time for qualifying, Antonelli was able to shake off the incident and take second on the grid behind Russell despite not being able to finetune the car's set-up.

In the race Antonelli then suffered from a poor getaway with no battery power as he was swamped and dropped to sixth, but Mercedes' pace advantage was thus that he was able to make a controlled recovery to second.

"If something like that had happened to me last year, the rest of the weekend would probably have been very compromised," Antonelli reflected in Austin. "When you have one year of experience, one full year in Formula 1, you come back the next year and you just feel better. Things happen a bit more easily, let's say, also because you're not forcing them to happen as much.

"I kind of took a step back in that regard and just tried to focus on the important things and enjoy the process as much as possible. Definitely, mentally I've been in a much happier place this year compared to last season. And especially when you've been working with the same group of people for one year, going into year two is a big difference as well. You know how to move on together as a team, especially from difficult situations."

Ford wants its sales back to pre-pandemic levels, and it has a new approach that CEO Jim Farley hopes will get the company there: Make cars that are actually interesting. Wild concept, I know, but perhaps it is just crazy enough to work. From the Wall Street Journal :
Ford Motor expects to sell 5 million cars a year by early next decade, Chief Executive Jim Farley told workers this week, a sales volume the company hasn't reached since before the pandemic.

The company's global strategy turns on Farley's emphasis to no longer make "boring" vehicles, which for now has left it without the budget-friendly small sedans and SUVs it used to give priority to. Farley has said that making affordable vehicles remains a priority, however, and Ford is planning to launch five new models priced below $40,000 by the end of the decade, including an all-electric pickup truck.

Ford once decided to kill off nearly all its interesting cars in favor of making crossover slop, so this will be a reversal of that. Of course, the crossover slop got Ford to the sales numbers it's now trying to return to, so who knows what's best.

Michigan's race for Senate is a closely-watched one, and it's made headlines recently as (former?) Democrat Haley Stevens turned away from supporting her (former?) party-mate Abdul El-Sayed to go back Republican Mike Rogers. But within Michigan, there's another factor playing in voters' minds: The trade war with Canada. From Automotive News :
The Michigan seat is crucial for Democrats to get a Senate majority. It's also a race where Trump's trade war with Canada has become a ballot box issue.

While most haunted houses will shutter until next, there's a year-round show sitting in your garage just waiting for another surprise performance when you're sitting behind the wheel.

We asked our readers last week about the most haunted cars they've ever bought . Responders filled the comments section with technical issues that I've honestly never seen before, like pop-up headlights that would erratically go up and down only in the rain. Speaking of water, there was even a boat that seemed to want to destroy itself out on the water. These are the kinds of problems that would haunt anyone's dreams. Without further ado, here are the vehicles most likely to have a connection to the supernatural:

My 2017 Chevrolet Volt was pretty much one thing after the other. AC only blew cold whenever it wanted to. Nagging "shift to park" messages even though I already put the car in park. A misfire. But the worst was when the car suddenly stopped and wouldn't move again, leaving me stranded in a parking garage at midnight. When I got it towed to the dealer, they traced it to a panel of wires that mysteriously burnt. The employees literally told me they had "never seen that in their life". The car was in the shop for three months because the dealer also said GM doesn't make the problem part anymore so they had to build one from scratch. I decided I was done with the car after that and got rid of it.

More cursed than haunted. My former car was a 2020 S560. Amazing car. Loved it. But I got hit in 3 separate minor accidents in 15 months. Never my fault – one while parked for gods sake. Each time requiring all the effort of insurance adjusters, body shops, etc. Prior to that car, I had been in one accident in about 32 years of driving (also not my fault). Traded for a 2025 S580e and love it even more – hopefully the curse didn't transfer.
Ps. How much you think a S-class with 3 accidents on the carfax is worth? Not much is correct :(

I owned an '88 Prelude Si back in college (think 1997) had been in a collision somewhere near the fusebox, and when it rained the popup headlights would alternate up and down (one up, one down, back and forth). I got really good at jumping out in the rain and pulling the exact fuse necessary to stop it, and then twist the headlights into the "up" position. I could have just left them up all the time, but the car looked SO much better with them down.

My dad and I rebuilt a 1960 Chevy El Camino for me to drive. I loved that car and was directly involved in everything we did to get it back on the road. Installing a new engine, replacing the clutch, sculpting the bondo to cover all the rust, and laying down the Corvette red paint.
She never let me down. Always got me where I was going.

In years past, Musk’s seal of approval would be a planet-saving badge of climate action honor for candidates seeking office. Coincidentally or not, Elon Musk’s highly personal vendetta against transgender rights has materialized against the backdrop of a corresponding focus in Republican Party campaign strategy, with one early hint being his “pronouns suck” message on Twitter in July of 2020.
Musk went on to buy Twitter and rename it “X” in 2022, and the rest is transphobic history .

Also coincidentally or not, the Republican Party has been hammering against human and civil rights for generations, but the razor-sharp focus on transgender persons did not bloom into full flower until 2021, after US President Donald Trump lost his first bid for re-election.

In the aftermath of Trump’s failed insurrection of January 6, the Party alighted upon transgender rights as a powerful tool in a coordinated campaign strategy aimed at ginning up the fevered emotions of voters already besotted with US President Trump’s “MAGA” propaganda during his first term in office.

In addition to working the conservative aisle of the US Supreme Court, the anti-transgender movement has focused on legislation introduced by state lawmakers (looking at you, Florida ). Among the LGBTQ+ organizations tracking the bills is the organization is the Human Rights Campaign, which has identified a distinct shift in anti-transgender strategy during the 2020 campaign cycle.

All else being equal, transgender persons are an unlikely target for a national political campaign. According to one study, self-identified transgender persons over the age of 13 make up just 1% of the US population , with much of the self-reporting cohort under age 35. As for the much-ballyhooed danger of transgender-related surgery on minors, that is vanishingly rare to the point of not occurring at all according to a 2024 Harvard study. Somewhat ironically, the same study found a “substantially higher” rate of sex-affirming surgery among non-transgender minors and adults .
For that matter, Elon Musk is known to have availed himself of body-affirming treatments as an adult, but that’s a whole ‘nother can of worms.

article_paragraphs: Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades.
It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.
Lexus confirmed the new vehicle will be made at its new manufacturing plant in Jinshan, Shanghai, and will go on sale in 2027.
As the first Lexus factory built from scratch overseas, the company said the new plant will bring together its global manufacturing capabilities.

Toyota broke ground on the facility in June 2025, saying the new facility will unlock “Lexus speed” as it aims to keep pace with domestic brands like BYD. Construction was expected to be completed this past August, with the first vehicle scheduled to roll off the assembly line in the fall of 2027.
The first Lexus model will be an electric SUV, produced using advanced manufacturing methods such as gigacasting to reduce costs and speed up output.
The facility will be a cornerstone of Toyota’s comeback plans in China, where it’s struggled to compete with local brands.
Production capacity will be around 1,000 units per month in 2027 as Toyota ramps up to “tens of thousands” in 2028.

article_paragraphs: Formula 1’s new world champion Kimi Antonelli has “made everyone look silly” in 2026, according to outgoing champion Lando Norris.

Antonelli became the 2026 champion by finishing third in the Mexican Grand Prix and his title celebrations were playing out on screens next to where drivers were conducting their post-race media debriefs.
There was plenty of praise from his F1 rivals and genuine appreciation for what he’s been able to achieve this year.
“Unbelievable, what he’s done; he’s blown everyone away. I hope everyone gives him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” Norris said.

“He’s made everyone else look silly. He’s driven that well, and he’s been able to click with his car. He’s worked hard to understand how to drive this car, and he’s exploited it better than anyone else. He deserves every single bit of success. He deserves these moments he’s doing now and celebrating.

“It’s even more impressive that it’s only his second season in Formula 1. He’s 20 years old. It’s incredible. I’m very happy for him. I’m very happy to see my number one go over to him, because he deserves it. I’m, in a way, happy to see it go.”
Norris added: “He has a very strong team-mate [George Russell], but he’s beaten him the whole time, the whole season.

“[You can] count how many mistakes he’s made this season - I don’t even think you could put it on [all five fingers of] one hand, honestly. He’s come from the back of the grid. He’s won from the front. He’s done everything he needs to do. He’s been there every single race. That’s something that no other driver can say they’ve done this season.

title: Electric trucks hit 50% of China's heavy truck sales, diesel demand falls
raw_summary: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%. And it’s showing up in the oil data. China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, and trucks running on batteries and natural gas are doing most of the work.
summary: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%. And it’s showing up in the oil data.
article_paragraphs: Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%.
And it’s showing up in the oil data. China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, and trucks running on batteries and natural gas are doing most of the work.
In 2024, new-energy vehicles accounted for 13.6% of heavy trucks (12 tonnes and up) sold in China. In 2025, sales nearly tripled to 231,100 units, up 182%, for a 28.9% share.
December 2025 hit 53.9%, but that was a rush. Buyers piled in before trade-in subsidies expired and new purchase tax costs kicked in, and the share dropped back to about 23% by March.

Then it came right back. Through the first nine months of 2026, China sold 226,400 electric heavy trucks, up 64%, for a 38.1% share. That’s already almost as many as in all of 2025, with a quarter still to go. In tractors, the big rigs that pull long-haul trailers, the September share hit 64.5%.

That’s well ahead of Beijing’s own plan. This year, 11 government bodies set a target of 40% new-energy heavy-truck sales by 2030, along with 1.6 million of them on the road, 30,000 km of zero-carbon freight corridors and about 3,000 charging and swap stations. The market blew past that sales target four years early on a monthly basis, and CATL now says new-energy trucks will be half of China’s annual truck sales by 2028.
It comes down to cost. In most uses, an electric heavy truck in China is now cheaper to own and run than a diesel one, and fleets run that math every day.

CATL claims savings of about 0.6 yuan per km. Independent numbers are more measured, but still favorable: a study by the ICCT and China’s CATARC found battery-electric trucks about 19% cheaper per tonne-km than diesel in good conditions, though they lose that edge at low annual mileage or when battery weight eats into payload.

raw_title: Cybertruck Could Get Trick Suspension-Based Loading Ramp
title: Cybertruck Could Get Trick Suspension-Based Loading Ramp
raw_summary: Loading a truck can be tricky if the cargo is heavy or awkward, like with a motorcycle. Tesla might have a novel solution, based on a patent application published a week ago that puts the trick suspension system in the Cybertruck — including the new low-cost model — to work. At the owner's command, it would raise the front of the truck, lower the rear, and make access to the bed that much easier. Patent application number US 2026/0326744 A1, titled 'Adjustable Suspension For A Vehicle', details a 'ramp mode' that independently adjusts the suspension at each wheel. The drawings use the familiar wedge-shaped pickup, but it's worth noting that Tesla describes the technology broadly rather than exclusively for the Cybertruck. Tilting the truck changes the angle where a ramp would meet the bed, which could make loading an ATV or motorcycle easier. Tesla also says lowering the rear would allow owners to use a shorter ramp. In one example, the automaker proposes raising the front of the truck by 80 mm (3.1 inches) while lowering the rear by 70 mm (2.8 inches) to reduce the ramp-to-bed breakover angle.

article_paragraphs: Loading a truck can be tricky if the cargo is heavy or awkward, like with a motorcycle. Tesla might have a novel solution, based on a patent application published a week ago that puts the trick suspension system in the Cybertruck — including the new low-cost model — to work. At the owner's command, it would raise the front of the truck, lower the rear, and make access to the bed that much easier. Patent application number US 2026/0326744 A1, titled 'Adjustable Suspension For A Vehicle', details a 'ramp mode' that independently adjusts the suspension at each wheel.

The drawings use the familiar wedge-shaped pickup, but it's worth noting that Tesla describes the technology broadly rather than exclusively for the Cybertruck. Tilting the truck changes the angle where a ramp would meet the bed, which could make loading an ATV or motorcycle easier. Tesla also says lowering the rear would allow owners to use a shorter ramp. In one example, the automaker proposes raising the front of the truck by 80 mm (3.1 inches) while lowering the rear by 70 mm (2.8 inches) to reduce the ramp-to-bed breakover angle.

Tilting the bed sounds reasonable, but the payoff is in how much it changes the loading equation. According to Tesla, the angle where the ramp meets the bed could drop from 45–55 degrees to 20–30 degrees. Tesla says owners would be able to adjust individual corners of the suspension on uneven ground and control everything from an onboard interface or smartphone. Included safeguards would keep the vehicle in Park, automatically apply the parking brake, and prevent shifts into Drive, Reverse, or Neutral while 'ramp mode' is active.

Sensor inputs could block or delay a suspension adjustment if conditions make it unsuitable. Other proposed settings include a 'dump mode', which lowers all four corners to bring the truck bed within easier reach, and a leveling mode intended for activities such as camping or tailgating on uneven ground. Interestingly, in November 2019, Tesla filed a patent application for an adjustable vehicle suspension. It featured similar ideas, so in a way, this is the company simply continuing the slow march toward patent acquisition and potentially production.

Of course, a key point here is that this is just a patent application. Like plenty of other patent applications, there's no telling if this ever makes it into production. That said, when we uncovered patents for Tesla's fan-assisted suction system and adjustable rear spoiler for the Roadster around a month ago, the company confirmed both were slated for production during the wild Roadster demo in mid-October. Those were practical engineering exercises and this new way of loading a bed seems to follow in line.

title: Which Automaker Has The Coolest Model Names?
raw_summary: Many car enthusiasts tend to view their car more as a family member than an appliance . Cars take us to some of the most important events in our lives, to some of the most memorable places in our lives, and hell, for a lot of us, they're the second place we ever see right after we're thrust into human existence and we leave the hospitals where we were born. To me, family members have names , not alphanumeric codes , so I've always preferred when automakers give their cars proper names. Thankfully there have been scores of cool, memorable car names over the years, but we want to know which automaker you, dear Jalopnik reader, think has the coolest model names . There's no cutoff date for this one, mostly because I think a lot of the coolest model names have been discontinued or replaced with alphanumeric nonsense, so feel free to unearth some obscure carmaker that hasn't made a car in a century or something, as long as they had cool model names. Sound off in the comments section below!

In a rare change of pace, Lincoln went from using lame alphanumeric model names like MKZ and MKX to what I believe are the coolest model names in the industry. To clarify, the company started off with proper names for most of its models throughout the 20th century, but for some reason Lincoln decided to ditch those in the 2000s, which I lamented, even then as a child.

With current names like Corsair, Nautilus, Aviator, and Navigator, the modern lineup is stacked with heavy hitters, but Lincoln's classic names are really good, too. Of course there's also the classic Continental, and my beloved Zephyr. I don't know that I could honestly choose a favorite name from the brand — it would be a tie between Corsair, Nautilus, and Zephyr, which all evoke distinct pictures in my imagination.

Corsair makes me think of the Vought F4U Corsair warbird. Nautilus makes me think of the prehistoric undersea chambered mollusk that has barely evolved over the past couple million years, and Zephyr evokes images of Art Deco-era pie-in-the-sky inventions like early flying machines and trains. All of this imagery comes from the exciting and fascinating names given to Lincoln's cars, which is something that alphanumeric names just don't quite achieve in my brain. Okay, that's enough of my yapping, we're here for you! What automaker do you think has the coolest model names?

Now, Lectric is giving its flagship XP4 a fresh makeover with three new limited-edition versions, each sporting a unique color and a new collection of accessories and upgrades designed for different types of riders, from urban assault roles to conquering your favorite off-road fishing spots.

The new Lectric XP4 Limited Editions come in three flavors: District, (black) Jubilee (pink), and Ridge (green). Each is priced at $1,399 and includes a 750W motor, upgraded accessories, and a distinctive matte paint job. That’s just a $100 premium over the existing XP 750, yet comes with a whole new host of accessories designed specifically for each special edition model.
So while the underlying bike remains largely unchanged from the bones of the XP 750, the new packages are designed to make the XP4 even more useful straight out of the box.
The District edition is aimed squarely at urban commuters, sporting a stealthy Matte Black finish and an accessory package designed for daily transportation.

That includes two waterproof pannier bags, a redesigned LevelUp rear cargo rack, a heavy-duty bike lock, and an upgraded high-output headlight. There’s also a fast charger, suspension seat post with comfort saddle, and handlebar phone mount.
It’s essentially a ready-made commuter setup, particularly for riders looking to replace some of their car trips with an e-bike.

The Jubilee edition takes a more casual approach, arriving in a distinctive Matte Thistle colorway. Designed for neighborhood cruising, weekend errands, and trips to the local farmers market, it swaps the commuter-focused panniers for a front and rear cargo package and a small roll-top bag.

title: Kimi Antonelli Becomes Youngest-Ever F1 World Champion
raw_summary: For the first time since 1953, an Italian is the F1 World Drivers' Champion. Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, clinching the championship. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010. With Antonelli never crossing the finish line lower than fifth so far this season, the ninth-place finish he needed to secure his maiden title seemed like a cakewalk. However, nothing is ever guaranteed in Formula 1. Antonelli was never in contention for the win at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez , but that didn't matter. His main goal was getting home in one piece. The young Italian qualified fourth and stayed there before cycling to the lead during the pit stop. He would eventually have to yield the position to make his own stop on Lap 43. He could've held the lead if he stayed out on lap longer. Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac suffered a catastrophic left-front suspension failure while heading into Turn 1. The machine became a sled, slid through the run-off area and slammed into the barrier. It took a while for Bottas to get out of the cockpit, but he walked away. Race control was forced to throw a red flag to recover his car.
