The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010.
article_paragraphs: For the first time since 1953, an Italian is the F1 World Drivers' Champion. Kimi Antonelli finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, clinching the championship. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver also became F1's youngest-ever champion, surpassing the mark set by a 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel in 2010. With Antonelli never crossing the finish line lower than fifth so far this season, the ninth-place finish he needed to secure his maiden title seemed like a cakewalk. However, nothing is ever guaranteed in Formula 1.

Antonelli was never in contention for the win at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez , but that didn't matter. His main goal was getting home in one piece. The young Italian qualified fourth and stayed there before cycling to the lead during the pit stop. He would eventually have to yield the position to make his own stop on Lap 43. He could've held the lead if he stayed out on lap longer. Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac suffered a catastrophic left-front suspension failure while heading into Turn 1. The machine became a sled, slid through the run-off area and slammed into the barrier. It took a while for Bottas to get out of the cockpit, but he walked away. Race control was forced to throw a red flag to recover his car.

Back in fourth for the standing restart, Antonelli took advantage of Charles Leclerc locking up into Turn 1 to snag the final podium spot. He may have finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton , but the celebration under a blizzard of confetti might be the most memorable of the Italian's entire career. After the trophies were handed out and the champagne sprayed, Hamilton and Verstappen hoisted the new champion up onto their shoulders in front of the roaring crowd. It was the Hollywood freeze-frame ending to Antonelli's meteoric ascent to racing's highest summit.

It was a disastrous day on the other side of the garage. George Russell started 2nd, but had a power unit deployment issue on the opening run to Turn 1 and sank down the order. He then made contact with Isack Hadjar in Turn 6 and received a ten-second penalty for his trouble. Russell salvaged a sixth-place finish. While the British driver didn't hesitate to congratulate Antonelli after they climbed out of their cars, it was clear he was devastated to lose the championship to his teammate. Russell skipped the mandatory post-race media interviews. In Russell's absence, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff heaped praise on Antonelli and the team's patience with the sophomore champion, saying:

"People said he shouldn't even be in F1, he should be at a smaller team, 10 races and no points, the tears in Spa, and then this. I'm just so proud for the team, all of them continued to trust him and he delivered."

The tumult at Scuderia Ferrari reached a new low. Ferrari seemed poised to take the victory with Lewis Hamilton taking his first pole since 2023. With how difficult it is to pass in Mexico City, the seven-time champion just needed to survive the start's lengthy run to Turn 1. His biggest threat turned out to be his own teammate. Leclerc slipstreamed from third to Hamilton, then tried to pass on the outside. The Monégasque driver took another shot at the lead heading into Turn 4.

Neither Ferrari driver kept their car on the track through Turn 4. While Hamilton re-entered the racing surface to make Turn 5, Leclerc cut the course across the grass to take the lead. Ferrari would ask the pair to swap positions to avoid a penalty, but this time was different. Max Verstappen had gotten past Hamilton. Ferrari and Leclerc opted to put their fates in the stewards' hands rather than yield the lead by choice. The decision: a five-second time penalty.

The penalty was enough for Verstappen to inherit the lead after pit stops, but not enough for Hamilton to take second. The decision's light-handedness was something Hamilton noted after the race, adding that he received a ten-second penalty for a similar infraction last year. He was far less calm during the red flag, telling his team over the radio, "We've got big problems. Big, big problems." After Hamilton returned to pit lane, he stormed off the back of the garage

raw_title: Giugiaro Revisits The Baby Lambo He Invented
title: Giugiaro Revisits The Baby Lambo He Invented
raw_summary: The Lamborghini Gallardo might have given way to the Huracan and the Temerario with its many variants , but it is remembered as one of Sant'Agata's most popular models that helped the company break through. The production supercar was introduced in 2003, but its development actually started in the '90s. Now, the designer of the concept — Fabrizio Giugiaro — has teamed up CAVËN Atelier to create a limited-production restomod. You might remember that the Gallardo was signed off by Luc Donckerwolke. However, its design was an evolution of the Calà concept from 1995, which was penned by Italdesign. Giugiaro had also created an early version of the Gallardo in 1998, which reportedly didn't change much as it transitioned to production. Fast forward to 2026 and CAVËN Atelier has unveiled a reworked version of the Italian supercar, giving its designer access to modern engineering, materials, and technology. The Hommage 26 is based on a Gallardo donor vehicle, adding a redesigned exterior, small interior tweaks, a revised suspension setup, and an upgraded V10 powertrain which is mated to a manual gearbox.

The production supercar was introduced in 2003, but its development actually started in the '90s.
article_paragraphs: The Lamborghini Gallardo might have given way to the Huracan and the Temerario with its many variants , but it is remembered as one of Sant'Agata's most popular models that helped the company break through. The production supercar was introduced in 2003, but its development actually started in the '90s. Now, the designer of the concept — Fabrizio Giugiaro — has teamed up CAVËN Atelier to create a limited-production restomod. You might remember that the Gallardo was signed off by Luc Donckerwolke.

However, its design was an evolution of the Calà concept from 1995, which was penned by Italdesign. Giugiaro had also created an early version of the Gallardo in 1998, which reportedly didn't change much as it transitioned to production. Fast forward to 2026 and CAVËN Atelier has unveiled a reworked version of the Italian supercar, giving its designer access to modern engineering, materials, and technology. The Hommage 26 is based on a Gallardo donor vehicle, adding a redesigned exterior, small interior tweaks, a revised suspension setup, and an upgraded V10 powertrain which is mated to a manual gearbox.

Visually, the supercar is instantly recognizable as a Gallardo, although most body panels are new and made of carbon fiber. The highlight is the connection between the headlights and the front bumper intakes, something that was not technically feasible at the time. Other notable changes include the pop-down headlight units, 20-inch alloy wheels, redesigned taillights with modern LED graphics, dual active rear spoilers, and dual exhaust pipes above a body-colored diffuser.

The interior looks similar to the donor vehicle, but gains small touches like Alcantara upholstery on the dashboard, a rear window that opens to enhance the audio experience, and a hexagon motif on the door cards with red stitching. Predictably, upgrades go deeper than skin. As reported by Classic Driver , CAVËN Atelier will offer the naturally-aspirated V10 engine with two different outputs, producing 540 and 560 horsepower, respectively. This is more than the 493 hp of the standard Gallardo but significantly less than the 907 hp of the electrified Temerario. More importantly, the engine is mated to a six-speed manual gearbox, which is not available in the Gallardo's successors.

The Hommage 26 was unveiled at the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, as the first chapter of the brand's Designer Series. CAVËN Atelier will build 25 examples, with a starting price of €900,000 ($1,008,800) excluding the donor vehicle. The latter currently ranges from around $75,000 to more than $500,000 depending on condition, meaning that the total price of the restomod could reach $1.5 million. The company has confirmed that similar projects are already in the works, with original designers revisiting models from the late '90s and early '00s.

The conversions will target collectors, given the steep pricing and limited production, but CAVËN Atelier insists they are intended to be driven rather than preserved in climate-controlled garages. What's interesting is that the Hommage 26 is not the first Gallardo restomod out there. The Etna supercar, from Tedson Motors, arrived in 2025 with modern design features and suspension components from the Super Trofeo racecar.

raw_title: At $7,500, Will This 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara Get Its Just Dessert?
title: At $7,500, Will This 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara Get Its Just Dessert?
raw_summary: Introduced in the 1940s, the Willys Jeep has long been hailed as the "truck that won the war." Let's see whether any of that DNA remains in today's Nice Price or No Dice Wrangler and, if so, whether its price wins our admiration. It's almost unheard of for an automobile model to switch from one end driving to the other, but that has happened on at least two occasions. The first time came in 1970 when Triumph released the Toledo, a model visually identical to the preceding FWD 1300, but featuring RWD under its twinsie bodywork. The Toledo went on to sire the legendary Dolomite Sprint, making that initially backward-seeming move a laudable decision. Another notable example of an existing model switching driving ends is the Polestar 2, which, with its 2024 refresh, changed its base single-motor layout from front- to rear-wheel-drive.

The Toledo went on to sire the legendary Dolomite Sprint, making that initially backward-seeming move a laudable decision. Another notable example of an existing model switching driving ends is the Polestar 2, which, with its 2024 refresh, changed its base single-motor layout from front- to rear-wheel-drive.

The 2024 Polestar 2 Long Range we looked at last Friday proved that point moot as the model offers dual motors driving both ends. It also had the model's biggest battery, a desirable driving assistance package, and, at $22,995, seemingly unfathomable depreciation. That latter affliction might be because Polestar sales are currently being banned in the U.S. due to the model's China origins, with owners possibly wanting out before the parts situation becomes dire. Regardless of threats of impending doom, our Polestar's condition and price had a number of you willing to take the chance—hypothetically, of course—earning the EV a respectable 66% 'Nice Price' win.

The name Sahara comes from Arabic, where it means "desert." Of course, that means we shouldn't call the world's largest non-polar desert the "Sahara Desert," since that is redundant. It's the same thing as calling Los Angeles' ancient fossil graveyard the "La Brea Tar Pits," since that is literally "The Tar Tar Pits."

Jeep chose the Sahara name for one of the myriad trim levels and special editions applied to the TJ Wrangler over its 10-year model run. The Sahara package included body-color fender extenders, full doors, cloth upholstery, and five-spoke alloy wheels.

This 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara is painted in Sienna Pearl matched to a gray hardtop and interior trim. Its running boards and outer bumper caps were likely once black but, due to the sun's daily attacks, have also faded to a similar gray hue. Other indicators of this Jeep's age include a cracked and dented right-front fender and rust bubbling through on both front wings. Fortunately, those are bolt-ons, and replacements are readily available from places like Amazon and eBay, making these aesthetic imperfections easy to address.

The rest of the Jeep appears to be in good condition, with the seller noting the frame and the rest of the bodywork are free of rust. That's a big deal, considering this TJ is offered in Pennsylvania, arguably the crusty buckle on the Rust Belt.

Another attractive aspect of this TJ is its removable hard top. Yes, removing or replacing the top is a job that'll take two (or three) people to complete, but it really makes this a four-season ride. The seller does warn, however, that while the A/C works fine, the heater is non-functional, so all passengers should be forewarned to bundle up in inclement weather.

The good news is that the evidence keeps piling up, and this latest example of electric endurance is a good one.

On the Out of Spec Renew YouTube channel , the crew took in a 2019 Chevy Bolt EV – one of the most affordable new EVs you could buy in 2019 – that had more than 470,000 miles on the clock and 330,000 miles on its post-recall battery. That’s nearly half a million miles on the original electric motor, and it’s still got more to go.

Out of Spec Renew replaced the 2019’s battery pack that was experiencing serious battery faults and cell-voltage imbalances with a stable, lower-mile example from a 2017 model. Once it was up and in, they got the car powered up, programmed, and driving again, putting the owner on track to reach the 500,000 mile milestone (sorry) in their trusty steed .

The OOSR crew paid $1,800 for the “new” battery, but estimates consumers would pay between $2,500-3,000 for the a similar pack. You can check out the full battery replacement video, below, then let us know how far you plan on taking your EV in the comments.

summary: The Trailfinder and the Trackfinder by Nismo Nick are two wildly different takes on the ladder-frame SUV for SEMA Following up on last year's V8-powered Xterra restomod , automotive enthusiast and builder Nicholas Scherr – also known as "Nismo Nick" – is returning to SEMA with a pair of custom Nissan SUVs.
article_paragraphs: The Trailfinder and the Trackfinder by Nismo Nick are two wildly different takes on the ladder-frame SUV for SEMA

Following up on last year's V8-powered Xterra restomod , automotive enthusiast and builder Nicholas Scherr – also known as "Nismo Nick" – is returning to SEMA with a pair of custom Nissan SUVs. The Trailfinder and Trackfinder celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Pathfinder, pushing the platform in two wildly opposing directions.

Instead of modifying the current iteration of the model, Nismo Nick chose the older R51 Pathfinder as the starting point for his unique creations. This makes sense at it was the last generation of the Pathfinder to ride on a rugged ladder frame chassis, before the nameplate switched to car-like unibody underpinnings.

As with the Projext X from last year, the new builds wear components from the current D41-generation Nissan Frontier, in a quest to modernize their appearance inside-out. Frontier-sourced parts include the grille, LED headlights, front fenders, front doors, LED taillights, dashboard, center console, and door panels.
Another common feature between the two is the Ruby Slate Pearl paint which is borrowed from the 2021 Nissan Maxima 40th Anniversary sedan.

Starting with the Trackfinder, it adds Nismo flavor to the Pathfinder, taking inspiration from the GMC Typhoon. The model sits closer to the ground, and rides on a new set of forged 20-inch wheels finished in black. Behind the then-spoke design we can see the cross-drilled and slotted brake discs clamped by red calipers.

Besides the Frontier face swap with glossy black trim and red accents, the Trackfinder gets special logos on the front doors, red and white stripes on the profile, a Seibon carbon fiber hood with a prominent scoop, a rear spoiler, and quadruple tailpipes sticking out of the rear bumper.

Power comes from a 4.0-liter V6 engine upgraded with a Z1 Off-Road supercharger, custom carbon fiber intake piping, a heat-shielded airbox, and an UpRev tune. As a result, the output has nearly double to a respectable 501 hp (374 kW / 508 PS). Another cool touch is the Xterra-sourced six-speed manual gearbox featuring a Centerforce clutch and flywheel.

article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton has criticised team-mate Charles Leclerc for his “do or die” attitude after Ferrari lost a straightforward victory at the Formula 1 Mexico Grand Prix.
The seven-time world champion started on pole at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez with Leclerc third, but he rose to second when George Russell lost momentum into Turn 1.
It was there that the Monegasque attacked Hamilton on the outside with the hope of completing it down the inside of Turn 2, but he instead ran over that kerb and remained second.
But it continued as Leclerc again made a move on his team-mate at the outside of Turn 4, yet space quickly disappeared and he took evasive action by cutting Turn 5 to gain the lead.
Hamilton was consequently overtaken by Max Verstappen , who subsequently took first due to Leclerc’s five-second penalty for the lap one fiasco, leading to the Red Bull driver winning.
The Briton ultimately finished second ahead of new world champion Kimi Antonelli, while Leclerc took fourth, meaning Ferrari remained on just two wins across the 2026 campaign.

A furious Hamilton said: “When I was at Mercedes , I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos [Sainz] several races, where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win.
“But it is one thing when that's happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That's significant.

article_paragraphs: As Ford prepares to launch a new generation of connected cars, the automaker is making a public promise about how it will handle that information.

The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automakers uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.

While those controls have existed for years now, Ford wants to communicate more clearly with its customers about them, especially ahead of the launch of new, more connected vehicles like the ones being built on its upcoming “universal electric vehicle” platform.

“I personally think that it’s super important for us to be making it very clear to our customers what our data practices are, and not only that, but making a commitment to them about it,” Ford’s chief privacy officer Kristin Jones said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I also see this as a great opportunity to educate our customers about how they share data.”

This new privacy push comes as automakers are making their cars increasingly connected. While some polling shows U.S. customers want the kinds of features enabled by this connectivity , such as remote start, navigation, and driver-assistance software, only 14% said they fully understand what data their vehicle collects.

That has left room for some companies to quietly sell that data to third parties — a practice that got General Motors in trouble with the Federal Trade Commission, and also resulted in a $220 million settlement with 36 states last week .

This lack of consumer awareness around data collection and sharing has also opened the door for other companies to market themselves as better stewards of customer data. Slate Auto, the EV startup backed by Jeff Bezos, has made that pitch ahead of the expected launch of its minimalist pickup truck later this year.

“We did a survey of 1,000 consumers, and 91% of them said that data privacy was a key consideration for them. Realistically, it’s not something they engage with every day, but they want to know that they’re, again, in control, and that they have access to the information they need there,” Jones said. “I wouldn’t comment on what our competitors are doing, or anything that’s sort of been in the news there, but certainly it’s something that people don’t trust companies to take care with their data, and we really want to make sure we’re building that trust relationship with them.”

If finding the cheapest car around is your top priority, then CarMax isn't going to be the best place to start your search. Every last vehicle in CarMax's national inventory has never experienced flood or frame damage, never has a salvage history, and never has odometer discrepancies. Every CarMax purchase includes a 10-day money-back guarantee, as well as at least a 30-day limited warranty, which may be longer depending on where you live. And they're all offered with CarMax's MaxCare warranty, which, for an extra cost, can extend up to five years after the purchase date on most cars.

I bought my 2017 Mini Cooper S four-door from CarMax in 2020, and I ended up buying the five-year extended warranty because I did not want to be on the hook for European car repair prices. Yes, the initial purchase price was higher than I would've paid at a normal dealership, or from a private party, but I really wanted the peace of mind provided by a warranty, and I have no regrets.

I ended up using the warranty several times over the course of my five-year contract, and I never had any trouble getting repairs covered, from replacing an engine mount to replacing a water pump to replacing a wobbly sunroof switch and a few other, smaller issues. title: How Europe's battery passport could have a big impact on US e-bikes
raw_summary: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime. And while the rules are European, their impact could eventually reach American e-bike riders, too.
summary: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime.
article_paragraphs: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime.
And while the rules are European, their impact could eventually reach American e-bike riders, too.

The battery passport requirement comes from the EU’s 2023 Batteries Regulation , which established new standards for battery sustainability, traceability, and transparency. The rules cover several categories of batteries, including those used in electric cars, electric bicycles, electric scooters, and other light electric vehicles.

Beginning February 18, 2027, newly placed batteries in these categories will need digital passports accessible through QR codes. Scanning the code will provide access to information about the battery, though exactly what users can see will depend on their authorization level.

The information can include details such as the battery’s manufacturer, chemistry, capacity, cycle count, carbon footprint, and materials used in its construction. The system also provides for information about battery performance and durability, including data related to battery health and degradation.

Anyone who has purchased a used electric bicycle knows that the battery is often one of the biggest unknowns. A bike might look nearly new, but its battery could have hundreds of charge cycles under its belt and significantly reduced capacity.
Even a quick test ride before a secondhand e-bike purchase may fail to demonstrate just how little capacity remains in a heavily used battery.
With replacement e-bike batteries costing hundreds of dollars, that’s a pretty important detail.

article_paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli is Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, aged just 20 and in only his second season on the grid.
Here's what we make of his achievement and his 2026 performance, our ripostes to some of his critics, and what we're hoping to see from Antonelli next.
There was never any doubt about Antonelli's pace potential, but for him to win the championship with few major errors is remarkable.
Aside from crashing in FP3 in Australia and clipping the inside wall at Turn 1 in Baku qualifying, he's been remarkably clean for a young driver in only his second season.

Yes, there are still rough edges to smooth out, as exhibited by his tendency to flirt dangerously with track limits. But that's something he's working on, and Austin showed he's making progress. And as he tidies up these aspects of his game and bolts it on to his underlying pace and the almost Fernando Alonso-esque relentlessness he can show in races he will become increasingly formidable.
That's what is remarkable about Antonelli's achievement. He's nowhere near the finished article he will become with more experience, but even in this unrefined form he's performed outstandingly.
Don't be fooled by the narrative some will spin about the crushing dominance of the Mercedes.

Yes, it's been the strongest all-round package, but team-mate George Russell's struggles prove that getting the best out of it and adapting to the new regulations is not easy. And Antonelli put an enormous amount of work into doing so on top of any advantage he may have had in default driving style over Russell.

raw_title: Car Design Has Gone Downhill Since The Plymouth Prowler
title: Car Design Has Gone Downhill Since The Plymouth Prowler
raw_summary: There must be something in the water, because there hasn't been a new car design in nearly 30 years that can even remotely be considered cool or fun . Most barely even scratch the surface of interesting these days. The most recent example I can think of when it comes to production cars that actually do something different at play with the visual form was the Plymouth Prowler of 1997. There wasn't anything like this on the road when it debuted in the late 1990s, and there still isn't today. The Prowler was a completely different way of looking at cars. Blending an element of retrofuturism and old-school hot-rod aesthetics, the Prowler was as much a baby boomer's fantasy as it was the car millennials drove in their adolescent dreams. Then-Chrysler Corporation lead designer Tom Gale was responsible for so many great designs of the era, including a trio of the most unusual concept cars of all time: Chrysler's Thunderbolt, Atlantic, and Phaeton. I don't know if Gale just saw the world differently than other designers, or was just capable of more than they were — his work on the sublime Lamborghini Diablo indicates this may be true — but in either case the Prowler was immediately a stunning piece of automotive history.

article_paragraphs: There must be something in the water, because there hasn't been a new car design in nearly 30 years that can even remotely be considered cool or fun . Most barely even scratch the surface of interesting these days. The most recent example I can think of when it comes to production cars that actually do something different at play with the visual form was the Plymouth Prowler of 1997. There wasn't anything like this on the road when it debuted in the late 1990s, and there still isn't today. The Prowler was a completely different way of looking at cars. Blending an element of retrofuturism and old-school hot-rod aesthetics, the Prowler was as much a baby boomer's fantasy as it was the car millennials drove in their adolescent dreams.

Then-Chrysler Corporation lead designer Tom Gale was responsible for so many great designs of the era, including a trio of the most unusual concept cars of all time: Chrysler's Thunderbolt, Atlantic, and Phaeton. I don't know if Gale just saw the world differently than other designers, or was just capable of more than they were — his work on the sublime Lamborghini Diablo indicates this may be true — but in either case the Prowler was immediately a stunning piece of automotive history.

Earlier in the 1990s, the Chrysler Corporation had launched the Dodge Viper, a study in function over form. That car was built exclusively to deliver hot nasty speed to its passengers. The Prowler was perhaps its foil, bringing the most style possible to the fight, but without any substance to back it up . For the purposes of this conversation, the substance doesn't matter. Prowler has style icon status and nothing has matched it, let alone beaten it, since. There are definitely cooler cars, but cooler looking? Fat chance.

I can admit that there's more to making a good car than making it look cool, but why aren't designers trying? The Prowler couldn't exist today for myriad reasons, but its spirit can soldier on to bring a bit more levity and flair to car design. Apparently everything has to be egg-shaped, with thin slitty LED headlights, thick A-pillars, and sharp, angular minimalism. And you can forget about a convertible at all, really, because allegedly nobody buys them.

Even car interior design has become little more than a minimalist dashboard with a large touchscreen in the middle . I wouldn't say the Prowler's interior looks nice by any stretch of the imagination, but at least it has a little fun with the genre. The color-matched binnacle and center-high-mounted gauges are absolutely ace. You can't beat a column-mounted tach, I mean, come on.

The Prowler was an attempt to do something completely different. Plymouth was on the ropes at the time anyway, so, to use a mixed sports metaphor, why not swing for the fences? What good is it to keep producing boring rebadged models until you fade away?

Maybe this was the beginning of the end for car design, as it brought about a wave of retro-inspired ripoff designs that brought nothing new to the table and suddenly became de rigueur. Or maybe it was so good a first shot that it never should have been tried again.

We've since seen 30 years of Mustang/Mini/Challenger/ID.Buzz-style returns to the same well for diminishing result. Plymouth isn't absolved of this, as it quickly pushed out the PT Cruiser in an effort to stave off death. The brand died anyway and its replica-retro-for-the-everyman car was stolen for Chrysler. Result? Nothing feels stylistically special anymore. When even Ferrari is farming its own history for retro-modern designs , it's time to hang up and try again. The trend has been taken too far, and we need to look for the next thing. Please. I'm begging you.

title: Piastri out of F1 Mexico GP points after post-race penalty for Lindblad clash
raw_summary: Oscar Piastri ’s tough Mexico Grand Prix weekend has ended in point-less fashion, after the McLaren Formula 1 driver copped a penalty for his collision with Arvid Lindblad . Piastri’s 60-strong streak of Q3 appearances (including sprints) ended at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as he qualified a lowly 12th, which paved the way for his troubles in the midfield.
summary: Oscar Piastri ’s tough Mexico Grand Prix weekend has ended in point-less fashion, after the McLaren Formula 1 driver copped a penalty for his collision with Arvid Lindblad . Piastri’s 60-strong streak of Q3 appearances (including sprints) ended at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as he qualified a lowly 12th, which paved the way for his troubles in the midfield.
article_paragraphs: Oscar Piastri ’s tough Mexico Grand Prix weekend has ended in point-less fashion, after the McLaren Formula 1 driver copped a penalty for his collision with Arvid Lindblad .
Piastri’s 60-strong streak of Q3 appearances (including sprints) ended at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as he qualified a lowly 12th, which paved the way for his troubles in the midfield.

Piastri did gain three spots at the start, subsequently overtaking Franco Colapinto and Lindblad to grab seventh place. The Australian led the rookie by 13 seconds when Valtteri Bottas crashed out, but the subsequent safety car and standing start reduced that gap to next to nothing – and Lindblad actually moved ahead at lights out.

Piastri pressured his rival for 12 laps before attacking him around the outside in Turn 1; now on the inside line for Turn 2, he didn’t back off early enough and hit the Racing Bulls ’ rear-left wheel with his front-right. Lindblad ended up in the wall.
“I tried to go up the inside actually, and then he shut the door very, very late,” the McLaren man recounted. “So I had to kind of avoid him and end up on the outside.

“I tried from there, and obviously he pushed me pretty wide, and at that point I knew I was not going to completely overtake. So I was trying to get out, but he pushed me so far wide that I couldn't go any further left, and we just interlocked wheels, and that was the end result, of course.”

Asked if he was far enough alongside that he should have been given racing room based on driving guidelines, Piastri responded: “It's always tricky. I was very close to alongside, and I was kind of there because I was avoiding a crash in the first place.

“A tricky one, but I think when we actually made contact, we were both going straight. It wasn't like I tried to stick my nose into Turn 2 and stuck my nose where I shouldn't. I was trying to concede the position, and I was already off the track, so I couldn't really do much more than that.”

article_paragraphs: Alpine drivers Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly have apologised for losing the team a double-points finish at Formula 1's Mexican Grand Prix as both picked up penalties for yellow flag infringements.

Colapinto and Gasly were eighth and 10th over the line and then promoted to seventh and ninth when Oscar Piastri was hit with a 10-second post-race time penalty for clashing with Arvid Lindblad at Turn 1.
But that haul of eight points has been lost because both drivers were deemed to have not followed yellow flag rules after Piastri's incident with Lindblad.
Colapinto picked up a 10-second time penalty for passing a single waved yellow flag and not slowing down enough.

Colapinto and Alpine "presented telemetry and photographic evidence claiming it demonstrated that [Colapinto] had complied with the regulations which state that the driver must reduce speed and be prepared to change direction".
However, this "failed to satisfy" the stewards that Colapinto had sufficiently reduced his speed when passing the single waved yellow flag.
He was cleared of speeding through the double-waved yellow flag in the previous sector because of "sufficient doubt that the driver had sufficient warning in order to comply with the requirements".
But the 10s penalty for his single waved yellow flag infringement dropped him to 15th.

raw_summary: Mercedes has been fined by Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards for George Russell not attending his media duties after the race in which team-mate Kimi Antonelli won the title. Russell failed to attend the media pen to speak to broadcasters and the written media.
summary: Mercedes has been fined by Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards for George Russell not attending his media duties after the race in which team-mate Kimi Antonelli won the title. Russell failed to attend the media pen to speak to broadcasters and the written media.
article_paragraphs: Mercedes has been fined by Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards for George Russell not attending his media duties after the race in which team-mate Kimi Antonelli won the title.
Russell failed to attend the media pen to speak to broadcasters and the written media.

This is required of every driver without a valid reason not to attend, as per Article B10.1.4e of the FIA’s F1 sporting regulations, so he was summoned to the stewards on Sunday evening, with Mercedes then given a €5000 fine.

Mercedes explained it excused Russell because he was "distraught" after the race. Russell had an energy deployment problem at the start of the race that sent him backwards from the front row. He collided with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar, picked up a 10-second time penalty for that and ended the race sixth, while Antonelli claimed a podium and the title Russell once hoped would be his.
Although Russell did not attend Mercedes’ celebrations, he did congratulate Antonelli and his family (pictured above) after the race.
"I saw George after the race on the FIA scales and obviously he's distraught about the situation," Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff explained.

"It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi. I have known George for such a long time. He is going through a hard time, but he was also responsible in getting the young man into this team.
"For a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment and maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season.

raw_title: 7 Luxury Vehicles From Throughout History That Used 4-Cylinder Engines
title: 7 Luxury Vehicles From Throughout History That Used 4-Cylinder Engines
raw_summary: Luxury cars can differ massively from one another, but most of us make similar assumptions when describing the term "luxury car." We picture leather seats, 20-plus-inch chrome wheels, full-size silhouettes, and big displacement engines with a lot of cylinders . However, every once in a while, automakers mix things up a little and throw in an ingredient you might not expect. Four-cylinder engines are one such ingredient, and they found themselves in luxury cars from an assortment of automakers, spanning across what is almost the entire history of the automobile so far. We're talking Fiats from the turn of the 20th century, British executive sedans produced by Rover in the late '60s and early '70s, hybridized BMW 5 Series sedans, Range Rover SUVs, and more. What's interesting here is that, for the most part, all of these cars were and are considered successes, with rare exceptions (Facel Vega Facellia, we're looking at you), which suggests luxury car buyers aren't actually all that hung up on the engine under the hood. Without further ado, here are our seven four-cylinder luxury cars, in chronological order.

What's interesting here is that, for the most part, all of these cars were and are considered successes, with rare exceptions (Facel Vega Facellia, we're looking at you), which suggests luxury car buyers aren't actually all that hung up on the engine under the hood. Without further ado, here are our seven four-cylinder luxury cars, in chronological order.

Today, Fiat busies itself with budget-oriented and retro-themed compacts mainly, such as the seemingly evergreen 500, plus its new and immensely cute Panda Grande . Wind the clock back just over 120 years to 1905, though, and Fiat was a very different automaker. It was at this point that it debuted its 60 HP model to rival equivalent models from Mercedes. This thunderously powerful car was powered by a 647-cubic-inch inline-4 with dual-chain drive and a four-speed manual transmission. A 60-horsepower inline-4 might not sound like much at all by today's standards, but in vintage car circles, this Fiat is sometimes considered to be the original supercar.

The Fiat 60 HP had a split personality, designed to be capable both as a road-going vehicle and indeed as a racer, with removable wings and advanced cooling systems. It was also mightily expensive, commanding a $13,500 price tag in 1905, while the sole surviving example also wears a $4,000 coachbuilt touring body.

The craftsmen responsible for the body used only the finest materials available, including aluminum panels, silver solder to cover and hide fastening points, and brass mouldings to disguise the seams of the wooden framework. As for the interior, it was about as luxurious as one could expect for a car of this era, with leather seats and mohair floor mats. Remember, just owning a car in the early 20th century was a mind-boggling luxury, let alone one of this caliber.

There is much that could be said about the Facel Vega Facellia that is wholly negative, but for a car so imposing and bold in design, that seems unfair, so we shall begin with its stronger points. Facel Vega knew how to do style and opulence quite well, and although the Facellia was its entry-level model, this experience is still luxurious. It was poised as an excellent alternative to Mercedes' SL series, or indeed an equally charming Alfa Romeo of the same era. Inside, the expected amenities are all there in the form of leather seats and numerous gauges set into a hand-painted woodgrain-effect dashboard. On the outside, there is plenty of brightwork to enjoy, and the Facellia shares much in common stylistically with its bigger brother, the HK500.

However, what it sadly doesn't share with the HK500 is its hulking great Chrysler V8. Instead, the Facellia sported a notoriously unreliable French unit – a 115-hp 1.6-liter inline-4. It suffered from overheating issues, fragile internals, and troublesome chromed cylinder liners, which resulted in the majority of cars experiencing engine failure within the first six months of ownership. Facel Vega had no choice but to replace these engines free of charge, but those second engines didn't prove much better either. A final resolution came in the form of a genuinely bulletproof Volvo lump, but by this point, the firm's reputation was in the gutter, and the Facellia would ultimately prove a hurdle too high for the automaker.

This is a far more conventional offering than the other two covered so far. It replaced the aging P4 model in 1963, and production continued until 1977, so it was clearly a popular choice. With it, Rover successfully filled a notable gap in the UK's car market, where simple commuter cars generally sat at or below 1.5 liters in displacement, while large luxury models sported 3.0 liters or more. With its 2.0-liter inline-4, the P6 could jump between the two segments, offering a premium executive model that cost less than the larger luxury products.

title: Can One Tire Really Do It All? 8 All-Weather Tires Compete To Find Out
raw_summary: Generally speaking, no one can have it all, and no one thing can do it all. That's just not how life works. And for the longest time, that was true of tires. You basically had to pick summer performance, winter performance, or disappointing so-called "all-seasons." Like with engines, though, tire technology advances, and the latest crop of all-weather tires claims to pretty much be able to do it all. But can a single tire really handle every single situation well? Our friends at Tyre Reviews compared eight of them to find out. The newest tire in the comparison is the Continental SecureContact AW, and when it comes to premium tires, a lot of times the newest one is the best. But is that the case here? Well, Tyre Reviews put it up against Michelin's legendary CrossClimate2, the Goodyear Assurance WeatherReady 2, Bridgestone's WeatherPeak, the Pirelli Cinturato WeatherActive, the Hankook Weatherflex GT, the Falken Aklimate, and the Atturo AZ810. And while this is supposedly a Continental-focused comparison, those of you who keep a sharp eye on Jalopnik's tire coverage will recognize that this is also an important comparison test for the much-improved Bridgestone WeatherPeak .

And while this is supposedly a Continental-focused comparison, those of you who keep a sharp eye on Jalopnik's tire coverage will recognize that this is also an important comparison test for the much-improved Bridgestone WeatherPeak .

Tyre Reviews is a YouTube channel that tests tires, then scores them in a variety of categories, weights each category based on how important it is for the comparison in question, and provides some of the best unbiased tire information on the internet. The U.S. doesn't always get every single tire Tyre Reviews tests, but we definitely get the Continental, as well as the Bridgestone. So how did they do?

In the snow handling test, well, I have some bad news for Continental and Bridgestone fans. The Michelin won. That said, the Continental came in second, and the Bridgestone placed fourth. But there's more to winter performance than snow handling, and the Continental edged out the Michelin in snow traction. There's also more to all-weather tires than winter performance, and Tyre Reviews' tests include handling, braking, and performance tests in wet conditions, as well as dry, and they measure factors like noise and rolling resistance, too.

Unfortunately for the Bridgestone, it just didn't have what it took to win this particular comparison. Or beat any of the other tires in the test. Oh, well. As for the Continental, it actually tied with the Michelin ... in first place. Each tire arrived at its first-place score differently, though, so if you want to see which all-weather tire is best for you, you're going to have to watch the video.

That's just not how life works.

article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton says the Ferrari Formula 1 team needs some "serious talks" behind the scenes after the opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc that he thinks cost his team a Mexican Grand Prix win .

Having started from pole position, Hamilton had kept his lead at the start through the opening sequence of corners, despite an initial challenge from his team-mate who had got up to second. However, he came under a fresh attack on the run to Turn 4.
As Leclerc attempted to go around the outside, the pair managed to outbrake themselves.

Leclerc ended up cutting across the grass and rejoining after Turn 5, having moved into the lead, while Hamilton ran wide at the Turn 4 exit and lost momentum – allowing Max Verstappen behind him to get past shortly afterwards.
That incident proved decisive as the five-second penalty that Leclerc picked up dropped him behind Verstappen at their first pitstops.

For the remainder of the race, which included a red flag and safety car restart, Hamilton was unable to find a way past Verstappen as he came home second on a day he felt Ferrari had the pace to do better.
Hamilton repeatedly throughout the race expressed his annoyance about Leclerc only picking up a five-second penalty for what he did.
And after finishing second to Verstappen, he felt the way that the events had cost Ferrari was something that needed to be discussed internally.

article_paragraphs: Toyota has Woodland , Honda has TrailSport , Subaru has Wilderness, and now Mitsubishi is getting into the off-road crossover game with what I feel like is the best suffix of them all: the 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition.

This will take the compact crossover's dirt prowess beyond that of the existing Trail Edition with a tweaked off-road mode for the all-wheel-drive system, a new "Rock" driving mode, and 18-inch off-road wheels with Nexen Roadian ATX all-terrain tires. That new Rock mode automatically turns on Hill Descent Control, uses brakes to minimize wheel-slip, and, Mitsubishi says, does so faster than it would in other drive modes.

A lot of the appeal of an off-road variant is in the aesthetics, and the Diamond Trail Outlander gets a blacked-out grille, darkened headlights, and redesigned bumpers front and rear, meant to improve approach and departure angles. The approach angle is now 20.5 degrees versus 18.3 with the standard Outlander, while the departure angle goes from 22.2 to 23.1 degrees.

Inside, a new water-repellent gray material can be found on the seats, held together by khaki stitching. The digital instrument cluster features a new page that shows off-road-relevant info like front-wheel steering angle, individual wheel-slip, and what the traction control is doing, while the multi-view camera system that lets you see where you should and shouldn't step can now remain on at speeds of up to 18.6 mph versus 6.2 mph in the regular Outlander.

Worth noting is the fact that Mitsubishi is debuting this car at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas next month, marking the first time Mitsubishi is making an appearance there since 2012 — to illustrate how long ago that was in Mitsu terms, the Evo X was still being made and would go on being sold for another four years. A stock Outlander Diamond Trail Edition will be on display alongside two other examples with increasingly extreme aftermarket off-road parts, and we can already hear that booth attendant unironically uttering the words, "It's amazing what a set of wheels and tires can do for these cars."

That name, though, may just be our favorite part of the whole package. Not only does it conjure up images of difficult ski hills, but diamonds actually mean something in the context of this particular brand. In Japanese, "mitsubishi" literally translates to three diamonds, as in the three diamonds that make up its logo. When it entered into a joint venture with Chrysler in 1985, that company was called Diamond-Star Motors (DSM). Mitsubishi once sold a car called the Diamante, and its in-house soccer team is called the Urawa Red Diamonds.

In other words, "Diamond Trail" is very much a Mitsubishi thing, and unlike, say, Nissan's Rock Creek , it isn't just two random outdoorsy words slapped together by some marketing people who thought they'd sound fine together. Diamond Trail also just sounds fun. Just self-serious enough, admittedly a little goofy, and very much imbuing the energy of a brand that — we say this with love — has little to lose.

In any case, Mitsubishi seemingly isn't done making Diamond Trail cars because it says this Outlander "will head a new generation of off-road-capable vehicles." As of right now, Mitsubishi only offers three other models in the U.S. that aren't the Outlander: the smaller Eclipse Cross crossover, the even smaller Outlander Sport crossover, and the Eclipse Sportback EV that's basically a rebadged Nissan Leaf . Hey, Mitsubishi, you know what'd be real cool? A Diamond Trail Edition of that cool new Pajero .

article_paragraphs: The Karma Eximius 1 is the first of nine one-offs featuring extensive styling and mechanical modifications

Karma Automotive has announced a new ultra-exclusive bespoke vehicle program, allowing nine special clients to create an equal number of one-offs with unique styling and mechanical modifications. The first member of the family is a track-focused model dubbed Eximius 1, featuring aggressive aero and a hybrid V8 powertrain.

The Eximius 1 looks like a beefed-up version of the Gyesera . The latter is the successor of the discontinued Revero, itself an evolution of the original Fisker Karma from 2011. The greenhouse, roofline, lights, and doors of the one-off are carried over from the donor vehicle, but everything else has changed.

The aggressive bodykit includes new front and rear bumpers with futuristic intakes and outlets, flanked by diagonal DRLs. These are joined by a vented hood, carbon fiber fender extensions, wider side skirts with aerodynamic fins, a complex diffuser, and a fixed rear spoiler. The body is painted in Borealis Blue with white graphics and exposed carbon fiber bits.

Inside, we find four Recaro bucket seats, Alcantara upholstery painted in Borealis Blue and Moondust, plus a generous amount of carbon fiber. There is also a motorsport-inspired emergency kill switch on the center console, and a custom carbon racing helmet mounted between the rear seats.

While the Gyesera has recently transitioned from a fully electric to a range-extender setup producing a combined 566 hp (422 kW / 574 PS), the Eximius 1 gets something more special. The model is powered by a series plug-in hybrid system centered around a 6.2-liter V8 engine which sounds like its coming from General Motors.

According to Karma, the powertrain has a combined output of around 1,200 hp, with 550 hp coming from the ICE and 650 hp from the electric motors. All this power allows the track-hungry four-seater to accelerate from 0-60 mph (0-96 km/h) in 2.7 seconds, before reaching a top speed of over 200 mph (322 km/h).

The one-off is presumably based on the aluminum spaceframe chassis that dates back to the Fisker days . Still, it benefits from a number of handling-focused modifications including a semi-active suspension by Öhlins, wider tracks, and carbon-ceramic brakes with two-piece slotted brake rotors behind the 21-inch magnesium wheels.

raw_summary: Sometimes, people will give serious things unserious names. A velvet ant, for example, may sound like a tiny critter that's covered in the sort of material you'd find in an old Land Rover's interior, but it actually has one of the most painful stings in the animal kingdom. Then there's the panhandle hooker: though it sounds like a questionably frisky profession, it actually refers to a dangerous storm that develops in the panhandles of Texas and Oklahoma. Or how about the Phantom Badger? We'd have thought it was a mischievous weasel that has a mask-like face, but no. It's actually the name of a military vehicle that was built by Boeing, in partnership with MSI Defense Solutions, starting in 2013. The Phantom Badger was designed to assist U.S. Marine and Air Force squads with a variety of tasks, including, but not limited to, casualty evacuation, reconnaissance missions, and search and rescue.

article_paragraphs: Sometimes, people will give serious things unserious names. A velvet ant, for example, may sound like a tiny critter that's covered in the sort of material you'd find in an old Land Rover's interior, but it actually has one of the most painful stings in the animal kingdom. Then there's the panhandle hooker: though it sounds like a questionably frisky profession, it actually refers to a dangerous storm that develops in the panhandles of Texas and Oklahoma.

Or how about the Phantom Badger? We'd have thought it was a mischievous weasel that has a mask-like face, but no. It's actually the name of a military vehicle that was built by Boeing, in partnership with MSI Defense Solutions, starting in 2013. The Phantom Badger was designed to assist U.S. Marine and Air Force squads with a variety of tasks, including, but not limited to, casualty evacuation, reconnaissance missions, and search and rescue.

This versatility is owed to its modular rear section, which allows the Phantom Badger to be quickly repurposed for different roles. It was also built to be easily transported in a Bell-Boeing V-22 Osprey, which is a popular aircraft used by the military.

The Phantom Badger's unclear fate makes exploring its specs even more interesting. While the Navy certified that the Phantom Badger could be transported inside a V-22, the vehicle was not selected for the U.S. Special Operations Command contract it was designed for. Records appear to show no evidence of the Phantom Badger being mass-produced for widespread military service.

As you might be led to believe, the Phantom Badger isn't powered by earthworms and vegetation. Instead, it uses a 3.0-liter multi-fuel V6 turbocharged engine producing up to 240 horsepower and 420 pound-feet of torque. Though we don't really know its 0-60 mph time, we can confirm it hit a maximum of 80 mph on paved surfaces. Its fuel tank is also big enough to provide around 450 miles of range, returning an estimated fuel economy of 21 miles per gallon.

In truth, those are respectable figures. Obviously, it's not quite as fast as a Ford GT Mk IV, the fastest American car to lap the Nürburgring , nor as comfortable as the Rolls-Royce Spectre Series II . But can either of those skip through waters up to three feet deep? We think not. Thanks to the Phantom Badger's height-adjustable suspension and 35-inch tires, not even a mountain of badgers wearing actual phantom masks could stop it.

It is both shorter than a Tesla Model S (180 inches versus 197 inches) and narrower (60 inches versus 86 inches). Now, we're not saying this thing will handle like an Integra R-swapped, left-hand drive Series 1 Lotus Elise , but its turning radius is solid at 24 feet. Staying true to its military makings, it weighs in at a beastly 7,850 pounds and boasts a 3,356-pound maximum payload.

The Phantom Badger has room for five soldiers: two at the front, two at the rear, and one in the middle. Plus, since it's an open-top vehicle, passengers aren't lacking headroom. Let's not forget that the Phantom Badger can hold a 12.7mm machine gun or a 40mm grenade launcher on its weapon mount. The rear hull sits between a pair of swivel stations too, so there are extra places for machine guns up to 7.62mm. Could the infamous honey badger have met its match with the Phantom Badger?

Dubbed the "King of Cool," McQueen was a hugely talented presence on-screen and unquestionably suave off it. He also had a genuine appreciation for cars and motorcycles.
article_paragraphs: Many celebrities and cultural icons claim to love cars and their engineering, but they don't know the first thing about either. McQueen, though, was different.

Dubbed the "King of Cool," McQueen was a hugely talented presence on-screen and unquestionably suave off it. He also had a genuine appreciation for cars and motorcycles. McQueen competed in various levels of motorsport throughout his years and was once even a road tester for Sports Illustrated. As you can imagine, his personal garage was pretty insane, with five vehicles selling for over $1 million at major auction houses.

One of McQueen's cars, his old Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S NART Spider, is heading to auction at Gooding Christie's upcoming New York event, which takes place from November 20 to 21 at the Javits Center in Midtown Manhattan. The Spider is projected to sell for anywhere between $15 million and $20 million, which actually isn't so insane considering the most expensive car ever sold at $143 million .

Ferrari built 10 examples of the NART Spider, and this car, number six, is one of only two finished in 'Blu Sera' (Evening Blue). McQueen purchased it sometime in 1967 and made several modifications soon after, including a darker metallic blue paint finish and reupholstered seat patterns. He also added a smaller motorsport-esque rearview mirror and a quick-fill gas cap, among other things.

It was already a true one-of-one car, but following an accident along the Pacific Coast Highway, which badly damaged the front and rear, McQueen saw further opportunity to customize. He took the car to famed automotive restorer and master painter, Hershel Conway of Junior's House of Color, who flared the fenders a little further and added the 'flip tail' upward-facing rear spoiler.

Oh, and if you're wondering about performance at this point, this diminutive drop-top beauty has around 300 hp in stock form courtesy of a 3.3-liter V12. That's the Ferrari 'Colombo' V12, to be specific, which is considered by many as one of the best engines of all time . If you get the changes right on the five-speed manual shifter, you'll hit 60 mph in just 6.7 seconds and pass a quarter-mile in 14.7 seconds. Remember: this car is almost six decades old.

McQueen sold the Spider in 1971 to designer, inventor, machinist, and amateur racer J. David Kopf, who sold it to NYC's Ferrari specialist, Grand Prix SSR, in 1985. There, the team reverted the Spider to its original Blu Sera paint and completed any other vital work necessary before it found a new home with collector and tech businessman Anthony Wang. It has been with him ever since, and is believed to have only been showcased twice — once in 1996, and another time in 2003.

This car has reached mythical status, given its rarity, history, and condition. We fully expect it to reach the estimated auction price, and then some. McQueen's Porsche 917K from "Le Mans" was previously sold for ... a lot of money, as did the 1926 Excelsior Super X motorcycle he used to ride around his ranch . So, what's stopping this one from landing an eye-watering hammer price? After all, who doesn't want such a significant piece of automotive history floating around their home?

title: Corvette Skidpad Grip Ranked Best To Worst Across Generations
raw_summary: The Chevrolet Corvette has been Detroit's answer to the European sports car for more than seventy years. Since 1953, it has gone through eight distinct generations. The idea behind the Corvette came from Harley Earl, former head of design at General Motors, who envisioned an affordable two-seat roadster that could stand beside the imports returning stateside with World War II veterans. The idea behind the Corvette came from Harley Earl, former head of design at General Motors, who envisioned an affordable two-seat roadster that could stand beside the imports returning stateside with World War II veterans. The first Corvette shipped with a six-cylinder engine, and it was Zora Arkus-Duntov (later nicknamed the " Father of the Corvette ") who pushed the car towards the V8 power it would become known for.

From there, the Corvette never stopped evolving. The front-engine layout that defined the nameplate for decades was finally abandoned when the eighth generation arrived with its engine behind the driver, a change that purists argued about — and the stopwatch quietly settled. What makes the Corvette so interesting is that it has always been judged by two audiences. One cares about straight-line muscle and badge pride. The other, which is usually more critical, cares about how a car handles when the road bends. And for a car built to take on Porsche, Jaguar, and Ferrari, that second audience matters just as much as the first — if not more.

That is where skidpad grip comes in. Measured in g-force, it shows how hard a car can corner before the tires let go of the road. This measurement largely sidesteps horsepower and driver skill (as you'll see throughout this article), instead mostly being affected by tires, suspension, and chassis balance. To keep the numbers easier to digest, this article leans on Car and Driver 's skidpad, which is 300 feet across in its modern tests and 200 feet in older ones. Other testers will be relied on only where necessary.

In terms of available and credible test results online, the C7 is where the front-engine Corvette actually peaked. On Car and Driver's 300-foot skidpad, the 2015 Z06 with the Z07 package "scorched the skidpad with 1.19 g." At the time, no production car had logged a higher figure on that pad. The Z06 also managed to stop in 128 feet from 70 mph to 0, cross the quarter mile in just 11 seconds at 126 mph, and do a 0 to 60 mph run in just 2.9 seconds.

Behind that number sat a supercharged 6.2-liter V8 rated at 650 horsepower, as well as Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 ZP tires. Weight-wise, the car itself is rated at 3,558 pounds. Car and Driver also posted impressive numbers with the 2017 Corvette Grand Sport, which managed to hold 1.18 g even with 190 fewer horsepower than the Z06, showing how engine strength doesn't matter as much as other factors for grip. Braking from 70 mph took 129 feet, the quarter-mile took 12.2 seconds, and 60 mph arrived in 3.8 seconds. And the Grand Sport is only slightly lighter than the Z06, tipping the scales at 3,452 pounds.

Interestingly, the Z06's 1.19 g is also higher than anything the C8 posted in Car and Driver's tests. Even the 1,064-horsepower 2025 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 managed a curiously low 1.13 g. In other words, the C7 Z06's 1.19 g is a measurement that no other Corvette generation could match.

The mid-engine C8 had every reason to beat the C7 here. It is the newer car, it has the newer rubber, and it has more horsepower across the board. The Z06's 5.5-liter flat-plane-crank V8 makes 670 horsepower, and the Z07 package has the car riding on Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 R tires. But on Car and Driver 's 300-foot skidpad, the Z07-equipped Z06 recorded 1.16 g. Chevrolet's own number for the car was 1.22 g, and Car and Driver noted that this result was "well below the company's estimate." The publication later explained that the Z07's tires had been inflated to the door-placard pressure rather than Chevrolet's lower track recommendation, potentially limiting its measured grip.

Regardless, even if we look at the rest of the lineup, the C8 failed to match the C7 in Car and Driver's tests. The non-Z07 version of the Z06 convertible hit 1.12 g, and the Stingray reached just 1.03 g. Later Car and Driver tests didn't move the number; as mentioned, the ZR1 reached 1.13 g, while the 1,250-horsepower ZR1X came in at 1.15 g. That leaves the C8 0.03 g behind the C7 Z06's result in Car and Driver's testing.

title: FIA explains controversial Leclerc penalty decision
raw_summary: The FIA Formula 1 stewards have explained why Charles Leclerc was only given a five-second penalty for cutting the track and passing Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico Grand Prix on the opening lap. The Ferrari team-mates were duelling for the front spot from the start, having already gone side by side through the opening sequence of corners when Leclerc made a move on the outside of Turn 4.
summary: The FIA Formula 1 stewards have explained why Charles Leclerc was only given a five-second penalty for cutting the track and passing Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico Grand Prix on the opening lap. The Ferrari team-mates were duelling for the front spot from the start, having already gone side by side through the opening sequence of corners when Leclerc made a move on the outside of Turn 4.
article_paragraphs: The FIA Formula 1 stewards have explained why Charles Leclerc was only given a five-second penalty for cutting the track and passing Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico Grand Prix on the opening lap.
The Ferrari team-mates were duelling for the front spot from the start, having already gone side by side through the opening sequence of corners when Leclerc made a move on the outside of Turn 4.
Both drivers braked as late as possible, with Leclerc running wide and cutting across the grass before rejoining at the front after Turn 5.
Behind him Hamilton, in his attempt to defend by braking late, had run slightly wide - costing him momentum which allowed the pursuing Max Verstappen to make a move and snatch second spot.
This area of the track was, like the first corners, subject to a special rule to avoid shenanigans on opening laps of drivers cutting across the grass to gain positions.

In a note sent to teams ahead of the race, following discussions in the drivers' briefing, the FIA said: "Any car leaving the track in these areas and maintaining a position to a car or cars within close proximity behind (as determined by the stewards) may be considered as gaining a lasting advantage, unless such position is yielded by Turn 4 [in the case of a car leaving the track in the area of Turns 1 to 3], or by Turn 12 [in the case of a car leaving the track in the area of Turns 4 to 6.]”
With Leclerc having not given up the place to Hamilton, he was therefore put under investigation for gaining an advantage – and it was decided that he would get a five-second penalty.

That proved controversial though with Hamilton in particular feeling that, with the advantage that Leclerc gained from having clean air which allowed him to build up a buffer, the sanction should have been the standard 10 seconds.

title: Dodge Entered The US Compact Truck Market Late With A Rebadged Mitsubishi Forte
raw_summary: Heading into the 1960s, Detroit's Big Three had begun to realize some folks preferred cars that were more agile and more efficient than the typically massive machines they were producing. Their response was to introduce a wave of home-grown compacts in 1960, led by GM's Chevrolet Corvair, the Chrysler Valiant, and the Ford Falcon. On the truck side of the ledger, though, things played out differently. Datsun had been exporting compact trucks to the West Coast since the first half of the 1960s, with Toyota following soon after. The Big Three at the time offered car-based trucks like the Corvair forward-control models and the Falcon-based ute-style Ranchero, but they didn't look like the real deal the way the Japanese mini-trucks did. The same year saw GM give that treatment to the Isuzu Faster, with the result being the Chevy LUV — a truck way ahead of its time .

article_paragraphs: Heading into the 1960s, Detroit's Big Three had begun to realize some folks preferred cars that were more agile and more efficient than the typically massive machines they were producing. Their response was to introduce a wave of home-grown compacts in 1960, led by GM's Chevrolet Corvair, the Chrysler Valiant, and the Ford Falcon.

On the truck side of the ledger, though, things played out differently. Datsun had been exporting compact trucks to the West Coast since the first half of the 1960s, with Toyota following soon after. The Big Three at the time offered car-based trucks like the Corvair forward-control models and the Falcon-based ute-style Ranchero, but they didn't look like the real deal the way the Japanese mini-trucks did. So when the mini-truck segment began taking off, the U.S. automakers went straight to the easiest option. Ford rebadged Mazda's B-series truck to sell as the Courier for 1972. The same year saw GM give that treatment to the Isuzu Faster, with the result being the Chevy LUV — a truck way ahead of its time .

As a result, the Courier and LUV, and their Japanese-branded rivals, were in the right place at the right time when the fuel crises of 1970s hit, starting in 1973. Chrysler's entry, though, was way behind. Based on the Mitsubishi Forte, the Dodge D-50 didn't debut until 1979, some seven years after the Courier and LUV. (To be clear, the D-50 would be renamed the Dodge Ram 50 in 1981, and Mitsubishi's Forte is unrelated to Kia's former compact sedan of the same name.)

Unlike today, compact pickups of the past were literally compact. So the 1979 Dodge D-50 pickup had a slightly smaller footprint than a 2026 Honda Civic sedan. The D-50 is 184.6 inches in length and 65 inches wide, while the Civic is 0.2 inches longer and 5.9 inches wider. As for a modern "compact" pickup, the Ford Maverick is 15.2 inches longer, 7.6 inches wider, and 8 inches taller.

The D-50's power train was likewise fairly small. The standard mill was a 2.0-liter overhead-cam inline-4 capable of 93 horsepower and 108 pound-feet of torque, and it was paired with a four-speed manual transmission. For the D-50 Sport, a 2.6-liter I4 with 105 horses and 139 lb-ft was standard with a five-speed automatic with overdrive. A three-speed automatic was optional with both versions.
More impressive was the D-50's maximum payload of 1,400 pounds. By 1981, when the D-50's payload rating reached 1,525 pounds, it could out-carry the '26 Maverick, which has a 1,500-pound payload.

The year 1981 further marked two other milestones for the Dodge. The first was a marketing change. Ram and Dodge aren't the same brand anymore , having split up in 2009, but they were still connected at the time. And in 1981, when Chrysler was readying its new truck lineup for the year, the decision was made to add the Ram name to the roster – transforming its compact into the Dodge Ram 50. The next year saw the Ram 50 welcome its first 4x4 configuration, complete with another new marketing move that positioned the truck as the Power Ram 50. The truck even offered a diesel power plant from 1983 to 1985.

The Dodge Ram 50 would go on to get a second generation in 1987, and that model would remain in production until 1994. Yet not only wasn't it the smallest Dodge pickup ever produced, it wasn't even the smallest Dodge pickup of its era. That honor goes to the Dodge Rampage.

raw_title: What The 'E' On A Manual Gear Shift Means (And When To Use It)
title: What The 'E' On A Manual Gear Shift Means (And When To Use It)
raw_summary: Long before our cars got fancy drive mode selectors, trick cylinder deactivation tech, and varying levels of hybrid assistance , automakers had to get creative with their engineering approach to satisfy the tightening fuel economy standards that arrived during the oil crisis of the late '70s and early '80s. Volkswagen's solution was a special manual gearbox design where the final shift gate was marked with a capital 'E'. The '3+E' and '4+E' setups found in the original VW Golf , Jetta, and the U.S.-spec Rabbit models had nothing to do with electrification. Many drivers at the time understandably assumed that the letter stood for 'Economy' or an 'Extra' gear. However, Volkswagen documents confirm that the magic word is 'Efficiency'. Rather than being a new designation for the fourth or fifth gears, the 'E' slot engaged an overdrive designed to lower engine speeds, minimize wear, and improve the fuel economy ratings at highway speeds.

article_paragraphs: Long before our cars got fancy drive mode selectors, trick cylinder deactivation tech, and varying levels of hybrid assistance , automakers had to get creative with their engineering approach to satisfy the tightening fuel economy standards that arrived during the oil crisis of the late '70s and early '80s. Volkswagen's solution was a special manual gearbox design where the final shift gate was marked with a capital 'E'.

The '3+E' and '4+E' setups found in the original VW Golf , Jetta, and the U.S.-spec Rabbit models had nothing to do with electrification. Many drivers at the time understandably assumed that the letter stood for 'Economy' or an 'Extra' gear. However, Volkswagen documents confirm that the magic word is 'Efficiency'. Rather than being a new designation for the fourth or fifth gears, the 'E' slot engaged an overdrive designed to lower engine speeds, minimize wear, and improve the fuel economy ratings at highway speeds.

The concept of overdrive wasn't new. Earlier British and European cars often relied on external electro-hydraulic units like the Laycock de Normanville system, which bolted onto the back of a conventional gearbox and was triggered by a dash switch or column stalk. Volkswagen's approach was different, integrating the tall overdrive ratio directly inside the transaxle's gear casing of its front-wheel-drive platform, and putting control on the manual shift lever. The '3+E' gearbox of the 1981 VW Rabbit LS was effectively a four-speed casing with wider spacing.

First, second, and third gears covered roughly 90% of all urban and B-road driving scenarios, while the 'E' gear was ideal for highway use thanks to its 0.70:1 overdrive ratio, running through a 3.89:1 final drive. While not a fuel economy record-breaking car by modern standards, when slipping the Rabbit into 'E', engine revs dropped to 2,500 rpm at 60 mph, boosting fuel efficiency from 24 mpg on the older four-speed up to 28 mpg, with highway figures reaching 42 mpg. However, this gear was best for holding a certain speed, meaning that drivers had to downshift in order to gain access to the full engine power.

In Europe, Volkswagen went a step further by introducing a special trim known as 'Formula E' (Formel E in German) across its entire lineup between 1981 and 1985. Not to be confused with modern battery-powered Formula E race cars , VW's system was instead focused on improving efficiency. It was available in the Polo, Golf, Jetta, Scirocco, Passat, and Santana, as well as the Audi 80 and 100 of the same era. The '4+E' transmission was combined with subtle aerodynamic tweaks and an early form of driver coaching.

An electro-vacuum computer monitored engine load against RPM and illuminated an amber arrow on the instrument cluster signaling the driver to upshift for optimum efficiency. After 1985, the introduction of electronic multi-point fuel injection, variable valve timing, and standardized five- and six-speed manual transmissions rendered these '3+E' and '4+E' setups obsolete. Engineers found ways to achieve superior real-world fuel economy without compromising drivability or forcing drivers to navigate massive gear gaps.
